sources.note: A second, deeper Contr experiment (distinct from and superseding the ID collision with the earlier model-separation KR-CONTR-MODELS/kr-contr-two-models-result): tests four candidate evaluation representations against 12 required distinctions, finding structured (value,reason) uniquely adequate (12/12) while flat candidates (A/B/C) each score 7/12, failing on unknown-family distinctions unrelated to contradiction itself. Written up formally in W-KR-CONTR-EVAL-2026-09.md (S2495, same batch).

rows.anchor: > **What evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the distinctions the KnowledgeOS programme has already declared important?**
rows.statement: W-KR-CONTR-2026-09 reframes the Contr question from 'three vs four values' to the deeper question of what evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the programme's already-declared-important distinctions.

experiment.hypothesis: a fourth contradiction value is necessary and sufficient to represent all required epistemic distinctions
experiment.setup: 12 required distinctions tested against four candidate evaluation representations
experiment.assumptions: the required-distinction set from prior Zero/Contr experiments
experiment.inputs: candidates A (fourth value), B (delegation), C (exclusive construction), D (structured value+reason)
experiment.method: pass/fail scoring of each candidate against all 12 required distinctions, plus a chromatic-number analysis of the required-distinction graph and an exhaustive minimum-representation search
experiment.result: A/B/C score 7/12 each, failing the identical seven distinctions (all in the unknown/boundary family, not contradiction); D scores 12/12; chi(G)=3; minimum representation is {value,reason} or {polarity,reason}, size 2, with reason indispensable
experiment.interpretation: a fourth flat value is not forced by the tested requirements; the obstruction is structural (a missing reason/boundary dimension), not cardinal (value-set size)
experiment.limitations: scoped to the tested candidate representation language and required-distinction set; does not resolve composition
experiment.conclusion: contradiction should not be represented as a distinguished scalar evaluation value; a structured (value,reason) representation is the surviving [EXP]/[PROP] candidate; Contr remains OPEN pending composition semantics

rows.anchor: * Candidate A — fourth value: **7/12** * Candidate B — delegation: **7/12** * Candidate C — exclusive construction: **7/12** * Candidate D — structured evaluation: **12/12**
rows.statement: Reports the core scoring result: A/B/C each pass only 7/12 required distinctions, failing on the identical seven; D (structured evaluation) passes all 12. The seven common failures collapse the unknown family (Unobservable≡InsufficientEvidence≡Underdetermined≡TheoryIncomplete≡...→U), meaning adding a contradiction value does not address distinctions lying outside the contradiction dimension.

rows.anchor:
$$
\chi(G)=3.
$$... **Given this particular required-distinction set and this adequacy criterion, at least three distinguishable flat classes are required.**
rows.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

$$

$$

with the two minimum representations: $$
\{\text{value},\text{reason}\}
$$

and $$
\{\text{polarity},\text{reason}\}.
$$

And: **reason is indispensable.**
rows.statement: The exhaustive minimum-representation search finds min|representation|=2, with two minimum representations {value,reason} and {polarity,reason}, establishing that reason is indispensable -- evaluation outcome is not value alone, EVal=(v,r) is the minimum representation found in the tested search space, kept explicitly [EXP]/[PROP] not a new KnowledgeOS primitive.

rows.anchor: Candidate C maps contradiction to `T`. Yet it passes invariants I1–I5. Why? Because those invariants test contradiction against the **unknown family**, rather than against satisfaction itself.
rows.statement: Candidate C (exclusive construction) maps Contradiction to T (Satisfied) yet passes invariants I1-I5, because those invariants only test Contr≠Unknown-family, not Contr≠Satisfied -- exposing a genuine coverage gap in the invariant suite itself, not merely a bad candidate; proposes I11: Contr≠Satisfied as a legitimate but not-yet-ratified [PROP] test-protocol addition, explicitly preserving the historical conflict (I1-I5 pass, capability guard fails) rather than retroactively declaring the suite complete.

rows.anchor:
### R_A

The first implementation unfairly returned `T` for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases... ### E7

The literal `"C"` detector accidentally matched context identifiers such as `C1/C2`.
rows.statement: Records two implementation self-corrections during the experiment: R_A, an initial implementation unfairly returned T for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases, corrected so all nine no-determinate-value conditions return U; E7, a literal 'C' contradiction detector accidentally matched context identifiers like C1/C2, corrected -- both classified as test-implementation defects, not candidate properties, caught by investigating rather than forcing expected results (E9).

rows.anchor: > **The experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar evaluation value. The tested adequacy requirement is satisfied by a structured representation in which at least one reason-like dimension is indispensable. The precise evaluation semantics, including the role of contradiction, remains OPEN.**
rows.statement: States the accepted formulation of the current Contr finding: the experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar value; a structured representation with an indispensable reason-like dimension satisfies the tested adequacy requirement; the precise evaluation semantics including contradiction's role remains OPEN -- explicitly weaker and safer than 'structured evaluation is the answer', since D is the surviving candidate, not yet the final theory.

rows.anchor: > What composition semantics, if any, preserves the distinctions required by the structured evaluation result without introducing distinctions that the corpus does not support?
rows.statement: Commissions KR-COMP-2026-09 with the primary question of what composition semantics preserves the structured-evaluation result's required distinctions without introducing unsupported ones; specifies ten minimum test dimensions (composition over value, over reason, over (value,reason), M3/M4 isomorphism persistence, contradiction-without-becoming-a-truth-value, whether U stays unitary or becomes reason-parameterized, Zero interaction, contradiction+missing-evaluator, +insufficient-evidence, +theory-incompleteness) and warns against selecting the composition algebra before enumerating candidates and constructing separating witnesses.

\neq
Boundary\ dimensionality.

rows.statement: States the nine-way collapse (uninterpreted, not-applicable, unobservable, insufficient evidence, underdetermined, theory-incomplete, etc. all collapsing to U) as evidence that Contradiction dimensionality is not the same as Boundary dimensionality -- adding a contradiction value does nothing to solve this collapse, an important result for Zero Lens.

Softens 'reason is the sole indispensable field' (since 'reason' could trivially be defined as Reason(x)=x, a disguised complete state identifier) to the safer claim that within the tested representation language, an explicit reason/boundary component is indispensable -- reframing the next question as what the minimal structured semantics of Reason actually is, more interesting than merely adding a reason field.

Eval(x)=(Status(x),Reason(x))
}
$$

rather than: $$
Eval(x)=Status(x).
$$
rows.statement: Proposes evaluation should be represented as Eval(x)=(Status(x),Reason(x)) rather than Status(x) alone, giving concrete examples (U,Unobservable) vs (U,Underdetermined) sharing top-level status but remaining distinguishable -- distinguishing Flat semantics Eval:X->V from Structured semantics Eval:X->V×R as a new research vocabulary distinction, and noting D is conceptually a product/structured evaluation space E=V×R, not simply a richer many-valued logic.

States a general methodological principle from the Candidate C failure: passing invariants does not imply semantic adequacy -- an invariant suite covering only one axis of separation (contradiction vs unknown) can miss another (contradiction vs satisfied) entirely, motivating I11 (Contr≠Satisfied) as a candidate, not yet canonical, invariant.

| Contradiction   | Unknown              |          YES |...Then the representation is tested against the matrix... $$
\chi(G)
$$ but **not the adequacy criterion itself**.
rows.statement: Proposes expressing evaluation requirements as an explicit pairwise-must-differ distinction matrix rather than a flat invariant list (making omissions visible, unlike I1, I2, I3...), with the chromatic-number calculation serving as a useful diagnostic on that matrix but not the adequacy criterion itself.

Connects the structured-evaluation result to the future ≡_sem work: two representations with identical final status (both Eval=U) need not be semantically equivalent if their Reason components differ and downstream operations can distinguish them -- Same Status does not imply Semantic Equivalence.

### FR-002

* `[EXP]` The tested contradiction requirements do not force a fourth flat value... * `[OPEN]` Zero semantics remain unresolved.
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate FR-002 freeze covering thirteen items from W-KR-CONTR-2026-09: tested requirements do not force a fourth flat value [EXP]; A/B/C fail the same seven distinctions [EXP]; the common failure lies in the unknown/boundary family not contradiction [EXP]; D separates all tested distinctions [EXP]; a structured reason/boundary component is indispensable in the tested language [EXP]; candidate C can map contradiction to Satisfied while passing I1-I5 [EXP]; Contr≠Satisfied is a required candidate invariant [PROP]; minimum flat cardinality is requirement-set dependent [EXP]; 'KnowledgeOS requires four-valued logic' is not supported [NEG]; minimal structured evaluation semantics, composition, canonical Contr representation, and Zero semantics all remain [OPEN] -- explicitly withholding freeze of the whole experiment until the 'reason is sole indispensable field' wording is re-checked.

rows.anchor: **Experimental Gate C — Structured Evaluation Required; protocol kernel designation K2. No KnowledgeOS kernel selected.**
rows.statement: Warns against the bare label 'Kernel K2' being misread as 'the KnowledgeOS Kernel has now been established K2'; recommends the explicit disambiguated label 'Experimental Gate C — Structured Evaluation Required; protocol kernel designation K2. No KnowledgeOS kernel selected.'

Final verdict of both reviews: ACCEPT WITH MINOR FORMAL CORRECTIONS; KnowledgeOS does not currently have evidence it needs four truth values, but does have evidence a flat evaluation value alone is insufficient for tested boundary distinctions; the emerging candidate is Evaluation=Status+TypedReason/Boundary, not 'KnowledgeOS=four-valued logic'; Theory v1.2 stays frozen, Contr stays OPEN, Composition is promoted to the immediate research target.

rows.anchor:
> **The obstruction is STRUCTURAL, not CARDINAL.**

The nine "no determinate value" conditions cannot be adequately represented by **any** flat value domain, **regardless of cardinality**.
rows.statement: Headline: the obstruction to representing contradiction is structural, not cardinal -- nine no-determinate-value conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality; A/B/C fail on the same distinctions, none involving contradiction itself, because they collapse the unknown family, not the contradiction family.

experiment.hypothesis: a fourth evaluation value is necessary and sufficient to adequately represent contradiction alongside the existing required distinctions
experiment.setup: formalizes adequacy as graph-colouring/injectivity: R:S->D adequate iff for all (x,y) in R_req, x≠y implies R(x)≠R(y); minimum flat domain size = chromatic number of the required-distinction graph
experiment.assumptions: R_req taken verbatim from the commissioning protocol's §9 table plus I1-I5, 12 required pairs over 11 conditions, not extended by this lane except in the explicit §11 sensitivity analysis
experiment.inputs: 21 semantic conditions across determinate/no-determinate-value/contradiction families; four candidate representations A (fourth value), B (delegated relation), C (exclusive construction), D (structured tuple)
experiment.method: deterministic witness suite (15 protocol cases + 2 more) scored against R_req; separation matrix over all 210 pairs; single-field ablation plus exhaustive 2^10 subset search for minimality; 20000-trial randomized stress test; required-set sensitivity analysis (S1-S4)
experiment.result: A/B/C separate 7/12 (same 5 failing pairs, all in the unknown family); D separates 12/12 and all 210 pairs; chi=3 on the protocol minimum, ranging to chi=21 at S4 (all 21 conditions mutually distinct); minimum adequate structure is a pair, 2 minimum sets ({value,reason},{polarity,reason}); reason alone achieves 11/12 (fails only Satisfied vs Unsatisfied) confirming it is a genuine non-trivial categorical field, not a disguised state identifier
experiment.interpretation: a fourth flat value is neither forced (chi=3) nor sufficient (no flat domain of any cardinality is adequate); the required-distinction set itself, not contradiction, is the actual modelling decision driving everything downstream
experiment.limitations: experimental minimality for the tested required-distinction set and candidate field language only; not a claim of universal necessity; contradiction's own formal definition (frame qualifier phi) remains an open decision
experiment.conclusion: Gate C: structured evaluation required; protocol kernel designation K2 (semantic state, not kernel operator); Theory v1.2 unchanged; next commissioned experiment is KR-COMP-2026-09

    R is ADEQUATE  ⟺  ∀ (x,y) ∈ ℛ_req .  x ≠ y  ⟹  R(x) ≠ R(y)
```

> ### The minimum flat domain size = **the chromatic number of the required-distinction graph.**
rows.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy as a pure injectivity/graph-colouring problem: R:S->D is adequate iff for all required-distinct pairs (x,y) in R_req, R(x)≠R(y); conditions joined by a required distinction form a graph whose chromatic number equals the minimum flat domain size -- making the protocol's §9 question exactly computable.

rows.anchor: > **`χ = 3` establishes ONLY:** *given this particular required-distinction set and this adequacy criterion, at least three distinguishable flat classes are required.*
rows.statement: Precisely scopes the chi=3 result: it establishes only that at least three flat classes are required given this particular required-distinction set and adequacy criterion; it does NOT establish that three values suffice semantically or that any flat domain is adequate at all (§9 proves none is) -- chi is a lower bound under one declared required set, and §11 shows that set is itself a modelling choice moving chi from 3 to 21.

rows.statement: The deterministic witness suite result: A, B, and C each separate exactly 7/12 required pairs and fail on the identical five pairs, all within the unknown family (none involving contradiction); D separates all 12/12. Over all 21 conditions (210 pairs), A and B use 4 distinct values, C uses 3 (folding contradiction onto T/F too), D uses 21 distinct values with zero collapsed pairs.

rows.anchor:
| `Contradiction ⇒ ¬Zero` | **FALSE** |
| `Zero_weak` on a contradictory state, under **A** and **B** | **closes** (`true`) |...> `[NEG]` **NEG-7. Contradiction does not merely fail to imply Zero — under both A and B a contradictory state CLOSES.**
rows.statement: Tests Zero interaction directly rather than assuming it: Contradiction does NOT imply not-Zero (false), and under both A and B, Zero_weak on a contradictory state actually closes (true) -- NEG-7, stronger than originally anticipated: contradiction doesn't merely fail to imply Zero, it actively produces closure. This reproduces D-0 in a new setting, confirming it is not an artifact of one model, and connects to KR-CONTR-MODELS' finding that the readings saturate.

rows.anchor: **`Contr ≠ Zero`** — invariant `I7` holds, but for an uncomfortable reason: they are different objects *because* contradiction produces closure rather than a gap.
rows.statement: Establishes I7 (Contr≠Zero) holds, but for an uncomfortable reason -- they differ because contradiction produces closure rather than a gap, not because Zero adequately captures contradiction; Zero remains a lens and must not become an evaluation value, and nothing in this experiment supports promoting it.

rows.anchor:
| fields necessary on single ablation | **`reason`** — and only `reason` |
| **minimum adequate size** | **2** |
| number of minimum sets | **2 — not unique** |
| the sets | **`{value, reason}`** and **`{polarity, reason}`** |
rows.statement: The exhaustive 2^10-subset minimality search finds minimum adequate representation size 2, with exactly two minimum sets {value,reason} and {polarity,reason} (not unique); single-field ablation shows reason is the only field necessary in isolation, with value/polarity interchangeable as its partner.

rows.anchor: > ### **Within the tested representation language and candidate fields, an explicit reason/boundary component is indispensable for separating the required distinctions.**
rows.statement: Softens 'reason is the sole indispensable field' (unsafe since reason could in principle encode arbitrarily much, e.g. Reason(x)=x makes indispensability vacuous) to 'within the tested representation language and candidate fields, an explicit reason/boundary component is indispensable' -- and explicitly tests rather than waves away the disguised-identifier objection in §9.1.

rows.anchor:
| **identity encoding?** | **NO** — 21 conditions, **10** distinct reason values |
| **does it collapse?** | **YES** — **66** pairs collapsed; a genuine categorical field |
| **adequate ALONE?** | **NO — 11/12.** It fails exactly one required pair |
rows.statement: Tests whether 'reason' is a genuine field or a disguised state identifier via three guards: it is not an identity encoding (21 conditions map to only 10 distinct reason values), it genuinely collapses information (66 pairs collapsed, confirming it is categorical not identity), and it is not adequate alone (11/12, failing exactly Satisfied vs Unsatisfied, both carrying reason=None) -- confirming reason and value/polarity divide labour cleanly: reason carries the entire 9-condition boundary family, value/polarity carries only the determinate T/F split, neither doing the other's work.

rows.anchor:
```
reason  ≟  (locus, modality)        locus    = WHERE the deficiency lies
                                    modality = WHAT KIND it is
```

| flat reason values → factored | **10 → 8** |
| **lossless?** | **NO** — 3 distinctions lost |
| **`(value, locus, modality)` adequate?** | **YES — 12/12** |
rows.statement: Tests a follow-on hypothesis that reason factors into two orthogonal sub-dimensions (locus=where the deficiency lies, modality=what kind it is): the 10 flat reason values factor to 8, losing 3 distinctions (Unknown/NotAssessed, Unknown/Uninterpreted, NotAssessed/Uninterpreted, all collapsing to agent/not-yet-done); (value,locus,modality) is adequate (12/12) for the current required set but not lossless with respect to the flat enumeration -- whether the lost distinctions matter is itself a required-set (R_req) decision, not an experimental question; the factor names carry no adopted authority.

rows.anchor: > `[INF]` **If the evaluation outcome is identical across a family, then no function of the outcome alone separates any pair in it. Hence no flat domain — of ANY cardinality — indexed by evaluation outcome is adequate.**
rows.statement: States the theorem that makes the structural (not cardinal) obstruction rigorous: since under the strongest candidate A all nine no-determinate-value conditions evaluate to the identical outcome U, no function of the outcome alone can separate any pair among them -- hence no flat domain of any cardinality indexed by evaluation outcome is adequate; of ten candidate fields, exactly reason separates all nine on its own.

rows.anchor:
| **S1** protocol minimum (§9 + `I1`–`I5`) | 12 | **3** | yes |
| S2 + the unknown family mutually distinct | 48 | **9** | yes |
| S3 + the contradiction family mutually distinct | 76 | **9** | yes |
| **S4** all 21 conditions mutually distinct | 210 | **21** | yes |
rows.statement: The required-set sensitivity analysis: chi ranges from 3 (protocol minimum S1) to 9 (S2/S3, unknown or contradiction family mutually distinct) to 21 (S4, all 21 conditions mutually distinct); a structured representation D is adequate across the ENTIRE range while no flat domain is adequate at the top of it -- the question 'how many values does contradiction need' is underdetermined not because the mathematics is hard but because the required-distinction set is itself an unmade modelling decision; choosing a value count before choosing the required set is choosing an answer before the question.

rows.anchor: | detect `Pos ∧ Neg` | `Represent` `Relate` `Discriminate` |...> ### Protocol kernel designation — **`K2`**... **No step required a power outside the candidate set, so contradiction is a SEMANTIC STATE, not a kernel operator.**
rows.statement: Kernel derivability analysis: every step (detecting Pos∧Neg via Represent/Relate/Discriminate, classifying subtype via Discriminate/Qualify, deciding resolution via Challenge/Determine, resolving via Revise/Select) is derivable from the existing candidate power set with no step requiring a new power -- contradiction is a semantic state, not a kernel operator (K2, not K1 since current representation cannot carry the needed distinctions, and not K3 since importance is not irreducibility); explicitly this is a protocol-scale designation, not a KnowledgeOS kernel selection.

rows.anchor: | **NEG-1** | **CONFIRMED.** `C` cannot distinguish contradiction subtypes: 10 family members → **2** classes...| **NEG-7** | **CONFIRMED and stronger than stated.**...
rows.statement: Full NEG-1..NEG-8 register: NEG-1 confirmed (C destroys all within-contradiction distinctions, 10->2 classes, all second-order combinations collapse to one value); NEG-2 not confirmed (D preserved all 12 required and all 210 pairs); NEG-3/NEG-4 partial (context/time matter for subtype but not decisive alone); NEG-5 confirmed (SourceConflict/EvidenceConflict/ModelConflict distinct from ClaimContradiction under D, identical under A/B/C); NEG-6 confirmed for A/C but B shows contradiction can live outside Sat without fixing anything (still fails on the unknown family); NEG-7 confirmed and stronger than anticipated (contradiction produces closure); NEG-8 confirmed for A/B/C (lose provenance/temporal distinctions entirely) but not for D's minimum pair, which retains them only because reason encodes them categorically, not because provenance survives as its own field.

rows.anchor:
> `[NEG]` **Candidate C maps `DirectContradiction` to `T` — indistinguishable from `Satisfied`.**

**And it satisfies invariants `I1`–`I5` while doing so.**
rows.statement: Reports an unanticipated ninth negative result: Candidate C maps DirectContradiction to T (indistinguishable from Satisfied) while satisfying invariants I1-I5, since all five only test contradiction against the unknown family and none forbids confusing it with satisfied -- the invariant set as specified is insufficient, and a candidate can pass every one while committing the most severe available error; caught only by the separate §19 capability guard, exposing that passing invariants does not equal semantic adequacy.

rows.anchor: > `[PROP]` **`I11` — `Contr(p,K) ≢ Satisfied(p,K)`.** A **test-protocol proposal**, legitimate but **`[PROP]` until independently ratified.** **A: pass · B: pass · C: FAIL · D: pass.**
rows.statement: Proposes I11 (Contr(p,K)≢Satisfied(p,K)) as a new candidate invariant, scored A:pass B:pass C:FAIL D:pass, explicitly kept [PROP] until independently ratified -- the invariant suite is not retroactively declared complete, and the I1-I5-pass/capability-guard-fail conflict is deliberately left unresolved (per protocol §37) rather than smoothed over.

rows.anchor: | **provenance** differs (S1 vs S2) | survives...| **retraction** | **does NOT survive**...| **supersession** | **does NOT survive**...| **context** differs | **survives as a distinct subtype**...`[OPEN]`
rows.statement: Tests the starting definition Contr(p,K) iff Pos(p,K)∧Neg(p,K) against seven perturbations: survives provenance differences (changes subtype not the fact) and confidence imbalance (.95 vs .10, not reducible to confidence); does NOT survive retraction or supersession (both distinguishable from current contradiction under D); context and time differences survive as distinct subtypes but whether they constitute contradiction at all is left OPEN as a modelling decision; model differences yield a distinct ModelConflict concept separable under D.

rows.anchor: > **`Pos ∧ Neg` is necessary but not sufficient.** It over-generates: it classifies retraction and supersession as contradiction. **The definition requires a currency/frame qualifier**, minimally `status = active`.
rows.statement: Concludes Pos∧Neg is necessary but not sufficient for Contr -- it over-generates by classifying retraction and supersession as contradiction; the definition requires at minimum a currency/frame qualifier (status=active); whether it further requires a common context and common time is left OPEN as a decision, not an experimental question.

rows.anchor:
```
[PROP]   Contr(p, K, φ)  ⟺  ∃ c₁,c₂ ∈ K .  active(c₁) ∧ active(c₂)
                                          ∧ prop(c₁)=prop(c₂)=p
                                          ∧ polarity(c₁) ≠ polarity(c₂)
                                          ∧ frame(c₁) ≈_φ frame(c₂)
```
rows.statement: Proposes a refined candidate formal definition incorporating the currency/frame requirement: Contr(p,K,phi) iff there exist active commitments c1,c2 in K with the same proposition p, opposed polarity, and frames agreeing under a frame qualifier phi (which of context/time/model/layer must agree) -- phi is explicitly [OPEN], a modelling decision not an experimental result. Also states EVal_min=(value|polarity, reason) and subtype(Contr)=f(provenance,layer,context,time,model) as [PROP] candidates.

type_signature.domain: proposition x epistemic state x frame qualifier

rows.anchor:
```
        Required Distinctions          ← the DECISION that sets everything (§11)
                 ↓
        Evaluation Representation      ← this experiment
...
        Contradiction  →  ONE particular required distinction
                          NOT the root of the chain
```
rows.statement: The review's most consequential structural point: Contr was being treated as a foundational/root item but is not one -- it is a single entry in the required-distinction set, itself set by an unmade decision (§11); the architecture reorganizes to Required Distinctions -> Evaluation Representation -> Typed Boundary/Reason -> Composition -> Aggregation -> Zero -> Determination, with Contradiction as one particular required distinction, not the root.

rows.anchor: > `[EXP]` **`Zero` cannot be defined before evaluation semantics are expressive enough to answer "`U` because *what*?"** The dependency is **`Sat → Zero`**, never the reverse.
rows.statement: Retrospectively explains why Zero resisted definition: the old Zero(K,I,EC)⟺Δ=∅ was underspecified because Sat itself was -- when Sat(r)=U one must ask 'U because what?' since U_unobservable is epistemically different from U_not-assessed; the dependency is Sat->Zero, never the reverse, confirmed from two independent directions (this experiment's §8, and KR-CONTR-MODELS §6's saturation finding).

rows.anchor:
> ### **`Contr` remains `OPEN`. What this experiment established is the SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM around it.**

rows.statement: Commissions (but does not run) KR-COMP-2026-09 with a two-sided primary question (preserve required distinctions AND not introduce unsupported ones -- both halves binding), ten minimum test dimensions, a preparatory Priest-extraction commission scoped precisely to semantic-value/composition/consequence/operation relationships (not 'what Priest says about four values'), and an explicit warning not to select the composition algebra first, citing KR-CONTR-MODELS §5's token-blind-rule mistake as the cautionary precedent.

rows.anchor: 1. **`R_A` returned `T` for uninterpreted and theory-incomplete states**...2. **The §10 detector matched the literal `"C"` inside context labels `C1`/`C2`**, making Candidate D appear to misfire on 47 % of states.
rows.statement: Records two implementation self-corrections: R_A's implementation unfairly returned T for uninterpreted/theory-incomplete states (fixed to return U whenever evaluation cannot run, re-modelling TheoryIncomplete via an evaluator_exists flag); the statistical-testing detector matched the literal string 'C' inside context labels like C1/C2, making D appear to misfire on 47% of states (a test defect, not a D defect; D's true rate is 0.0) -- both corrections applied before any reported figure.

rows.anchor: **The safer position is also the stronger one: KnowledgeOS has no evidence that it needs four truth values; it has evidence that a flat evaluation value alone is insufficient for the tested boundary distinctions.**
rows.statement: States the conclusion at its safe strength: the experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar value; a structured representation with at least one indispensable reason-like dimension satisfies the tested adequacy requirement; the precise evaluation semantics remain OPEN; D is the surviving tested candidate (making every alternative tested inadequate), not proven correct or final theory; EVal=(v,r) is [EXP]/[PROP], the minimum found in the tested search space, explicitly not a KnowledgeOS primitive to be cited as such.

Revises the implementation strategy from an FDE state model to a factorized evaluation model: Evaluation Representation = Status/Polarity × Typed Boundary/Reason, with FDE's two-channel structure as one candidate for the first factor only -- explicitly noting minimality/sufficiency of this factorization remains open.

rows.anchor: **Predecessor:** `KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09` — `E-FDE-5` established that composition and frame qualification are coupled. This experiment tests the coupling directly.
rows.statement: Records that KR-COMP-2026-09 was commissioned as a direct test of a coupling (composition and frame qualification) already established by a predecessor experiment KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09's result E-FDE-5 -- confirming the FDE-inspired implementation proposed in S2496/S2497 was actually executed, though its own write-up is not part of this batch.

rows.anchor:
( aggregation rule ,  frame qualifier φ ,  status policy )

swept over the **full cross-product — 5 × 6 × 3 = 90 combinations.** **No rule was selected in advance**
rows.statement: Commissions KR-COMP-2026-09 as a coupled-triple sweep (aggregation rule x frame qualifier phi x status policy, 5x6x3=90 combinations), rules enumerated before witnesses per KR-CONTR-EVAL §21.1's discipline, with status policy deliberately made a swept parameter to test whether supersession belongs to or before composition; pipeline: evidence -> [status policy] -> [partition by phi] -> [within-frame standing] -> [aggregate]; scored against five commission criteria C1-C5 (preserve genuine conflict, supersession is not conflict, preserve boundary distinctions, no false opposition, remain explicit about the frame).

experiment.hypothesis: a single composition rule can be chosen for aggregating epistemic standing across evidence, independent of any frame qualifier
experiment.setup: full 90-combination cross-product of 5 aggregation rules x 6 frame-qualifier settings x 3 status policies, each scored against 5 criteria with witnesses
experiment.assumptions: criteria C1-C5 as verbatim commissioned; no rule or phi selected in advance
experiment.inputs: union/majority/last-wins/strict/intraframe-only rules; phi in {∅,{time},{context},{layer},{time,context},{time,context,layer}}; filter/keep/demote status policies
experiment.method: deterministic exhaustive scoring of all 90 combinations against C1-C5, with a robustness re-run dropping the one operationally-stipulated criterion C5
experiment.result: 18/90 pass all five criteria, every passing combination has phi⊇{time,context}; three rules (majority, last-wins, intraframe-only) tie at 5/5 once phi is adequate; status policy is completely irrelevant (6/30 for all three); union and strict excluded for opposite reasons; dropping C5 changes nothing
experiment.interpretation: the criteria select a frame qualifier, not a composition rule -- inverting the expected shape of the question; supersession is a special case of temporal separation, not an independent mechanism, in the tested space
experiment.limitations: the surviving three rules are indistinguishable because the witness suite places all genuine contradictions inside a single frame; a witness with genuine conflict in one frame and divergence across others would be needed to separate them; phi's adequacy is scoped to tested witnesses
experiment.conclusion: phi is load-bearing and non-additive (neither time nor context alone suffices); the rule itself remains open pending a rule-separating witness; phi and R_req selection are both decisions, not experiments

rows.anchor:
> ### **18 of 90 combinations satisfy all five criteria.**
> ### **Every single one has `φ ⊇ {time, context}`.**
rows.statement: Headline result: 18/90 combinations pass all five criteria, and every single passing combination has phi containing at least {time,context}; phi=∅/{time}/{context}/{layer} alone each score 0/15, while {time,context} and {time,context,layer} each score 9/15.

rows.anchor: **You cannot choose the rule before φ**: the rule ranking changes with φ (2 distinct rankings). **But once `φ ⊇ {time, context}`, three rules tie at 5/5**
rows.statement: Confirms and sharpens E-FDE-5: composition and frame qualification are coupled, with the frame as the load-bearing half -- rule ranking depends on phi (2 distinct rankings across the phi settings), but once phi⊇{time,context}, majority/last-wins/intraframe-only are indistinguishable (tie at 5/5); the criteria therefore select a frame qualifier, not a composition rule, inverting the expected shape of the original question ('which composition rule?' becomes 'which frame qualifier?', with the rule reported as still open).

rows.anchor: **Why the surviving rules agree:** with a frame qualifier in force, **conflict is detected WITHIN a frame**...A suite that separated the rules would need a witness with genuine conflict in one frame and divergence across others — this one has none, and that is a limitation of the suite, not a result.
rows.statement: Explains why the three surviving rules agree: with a frame qualifier active, conflict is detected within a frame and the aggregation rule only governs across-frame behavior; the witness suite places all genuine contradictions inside a single frame so the across-frame policy never gets exercised -- explicitly identified as a limitation of the test suite, not a positive finding that the rules are equivalent in general.

rows.anchor:
> `[EXP]` **`{time}` alone: 0/15. `{context}` alone: 0/15. `{time, context}`: 9/15.**

...**`layer` is not required by any tested witness.**
rows.statement: Shows phi is non-additive: each feature is needed by a distinct witness (TemporalConflict needs time, ContextConflict needs context), so phi's adequacy is not a property of its individual features; adding layer on top of {time,context} changes nothing (still 9/15), meaning layer is not required by any tested witness (though not thereby shown unnecessary in general).

rows.anchor: > `[EXP]` **The status policy is completely irrelevant: `filter`, `keep` and `demote` all score 6/30.** Not "roughly equal" — **identical.**
rows.statement: Shows the status policy (filter/keep/demote) is completely irrelevant (identical 6/30 score for all three), because once time is in phi, superseded evidence sits in a different frame from what supersedes it regardless of status handling -- supersession is therefore not an independent mechanism in the tested space, it is a special case of temporal separation; a system with a time-based frame qualifier does not additionally need a supersession rule for THIS purpose, though whether it needs one for retirement/lifecycle purposes remains open.

rows.anchor: | **`union`** | **C3, C5** | it takes any positive and any negative **across** frames... | **`strict`** | **C1** | it maps conflict to "no support", **destroying the genuine positive/negative conflict**
rows.statement: Excludes union (fails C3/C5: collapses TemporalConflict and ContextConflict onto DirectContradiction by ignoring frame separation) and strict (fails C1: maps conflict to no-support, destroying the genuine conflict the representation exists to carry) for opposite reasons; resolves an apparent tension with the predecessor's 'only union produces a conflicting Standing' finding by noting that claim held only in the absence of a frame -- union is excluded precisely once a frame exists, while the surviving rules produce conflict within frames.

rows.anchor: **C5 (*"remain explicit about the evaluation frame"*) is the only criterion the commission stated conceptually rather than operationally.**...the sweep was re-run with **C5 dropped entirely**...**The verdict is unchanged. C5 contributes nothing to the exclusion.**
rows.statement: Performs a robustness check on the one criterion (C5) that had to be operationalized from a conceptual statement, since the operationalization (a stipulated clause failing phi=∅) could have manufactured the headline result; re-running the full sweep with C5 dropped entirely gives an identical verdict (18/90, same phi and rules), confirming phi=∅ and union are excluded by C3 alone on independent witnesses (TemporalConflict≡DirectContradiction, ContextConflict≡DirectContradiction) -- the stipulation was not doing the work. Also records a caught self-correction: an earlier C5 version ignored the passed phi and tested rule-level phi-sensitivity instead, letting 45/90 pass vacuously, corrected before any reported figure.

rows.anchor:
- **No composition rule is selected.** Three remain, and this suite cannot separate them.
- **`φ` is not settled.**...- **`ℛ_req` is not settled** — and it continues to set everything (fourth independent occurrence).
rows.statement: States explicitly what remains unsettled: no composition rule is selected (three remain tied); phi itself is not settled ({time,context} is only the smallest adequate qualifier over the tested witnesses; a different witness set could demand more, choosing phi is a decision); R_req is not settled and continues to set everything, now its fourth independent occurrence as the load-bearing modelling decision; Contr and Zero remain untouched; layer is not shown unnecessary, only not required by tested witnesses; nothing is adopted, Theory v1.2 unchanged, kernel NOT SELECTABLE.

rows.anchor: > `[PROP]` **A witness that separates the three surviving rules** — genuine conflict inside one frame **and** divergence across others. Until such a witness exists, *"which composition rule?"* is not an answerable question
rows.statement: Recommends next constructing a witness that separates the three surviving rules (genuine conflict inside one frame plus divergence across others) before 'which composition rule' can be answered, since asking it now would produce an arbitrary choice dressed as a result; separately, the phi decision and the R_req decision are both flagged as decisions (not experiments) -- the fourth and fifth items to reach that category, after factivity, M3≅M4, and 𝓑.

rows.statement: Extracts Ziem's U-relevance postulate (no understanding-relevant meaning aspect may be excluded merely because a theory's methodological premises are inconvenient) as a direct formal analogue of R_req: any representation that collapses a distinction required for understanding is inadequate regardless of its mathematical elegance.

rows.anchor: > ⚠️ **Boundary ambiguity affects EVERY `Standing` class, not only `(0,0)`.** `NotAssessed`, `Underdetermined` and `TheoryIncomplete` all sit in `(1,0)` — evidence *is* present, merely unevaluated, insufficient, or without an evaluator. **A positive Standing is as boundary-ambiguous as an empty one.**
rows.statement: States a genuinely new finding sharpening E-FDE-2/E-FDE-3: boundary ambiguity is not confined to the (0,0) no-support case -- NotAssessed, Underdetermined, and TheoryIncomplete all sit at (1,0) (evidence IS present but merely unevaluated, insufficient, or lacking an evaluator), so a positive Standing is exactly as boundary-ambiguous as an empty one, strengthening the case that the boundary/reason component is indispensable across the whole representation, not only at the (0,0) corner.

Proposes entailment-based content evaluation E_content(K,r) (T if K entails Content(r), F if K entails not-Content(r), U otherwise) as a candidate for the content dimension of evaluation only, explicitly constrained: this does not solve the standing/boundary problem, since the FDE work already showed U collapses several fundamentally different situations.

rows.statement: Section 9 (feeding FR-3/FR-4): distinguishes six typed causes of epistemic failure-to-derive -- U_rep (not represented), U_der (not derivable under S), U_avail (derivable but resource-unavailable), U_evid (insufficient evidence), U_eval (evaluation cannot determine), U_scope (outside declared scope) -- explicitly refusing to flatten them into one enum, per prior FDE/Zero experiments, and reaffirming the structured EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) direction as better than a flat value set. rows.anchor: [NEG] The successor-state axiom silently resolves gamma+ AND gamma- in favour of gamma+ -- measured, from both F true and F false. rows.statement: [NEG] The decisive limit: the Reiter successor-state axiom, measured from both F-true and F-false starting states, silently resolves a gamma+/gamma- conflict in favour of gamma+ -- it presupposes consistent effect axioms and cannot detect their inconsistency. Since the KnowledgeOS programme has spent four separate experiments specifically preventing this kind of silent collapse, the SSA is disqualified as a drop-in delta implementation, while remaining clarifying as a statement of a boundary: delta cannot be settled before Contr (contradiction handling) is settled.

assumptions.anchor: It presupposes consistent effect axioms; it cannot detect their inconsistency

experiment.hypothesis: the successor-state axiom handles gamma+/gamma- conflict safely
experiment.setup: measure SSA behaviour starting from F=true and from F=false
experiment.assumptions: consistent effect axioms (violated by construction in the test)
experiment.inputs: conflicting gamma+ and gamma- for the same fluent
experiment.method: direct measurement of SSA output under both starting truth values
experiment.result: SSA silently resolves in favour of gamma+ regardless of starting truth value
experiment.interpretation: the SSA cannot detect or flag inconsistent effect axioms; it always favours the positive effect
experiment.limitations: tested only for boolean fluents under one specific conflict shape
experiment.conclusion: SSA is disqualified as a drop-in for KnowledgeOS's delta while Contr is unresolved

rows.anchor: KR-CONTR-EVAL: the evaluation obstruction is structural, not cardinal -- no flat value domain of any cardinality is adequate. KR-CONTR-FDE: the surviving factorization is Status x Typed Boundary. KR-COMP: composition's load-bearing parameter is the frame qualifier, not the rule.
rows.statement: Restates three corpus-native results established before the Reiter source was read: KR-CONTR-EVAL found the evaluation obstruction is structural (not cardinal) -- no flat value domain of any cardinality is adequate; a distinctly-named KR-CONTR-FDE (relation to the indexed KR-CONTR-EVAL object unclear from this file alone) found the surviving contradiction factorization is Status x Typed Boundary; KR-COMP found composition's load-bearing parameter is the frame qualifier, not the composition rule itself.

rows.anchor: Part 6: The 'Failure to Derive' Distinction -- A critical consequence of FR-2, FR-3, and FR-4: U_rep, U_der, U_avail, U_evid, U_eval, U_scope. We do not flatten these into one enum. Instead EVal = (Value, Reason, Boundary, ...) remains the better direction.
rows.statement: Part 6 formalizes the six-way typed failure-to-derive distinction (U_rep, U_der, U_avail, U_evid, U_eval, U_scope) as a named critical consequence of FR-2/FR-3/FR-4 combined, explicitly not flattened into one enum, reaffirming EVal=(Value,Reason,Boundary,...) as the preferred structured direction.
invariants: the six failure-to-derive causes are not flattened into one enum

rows.anchor: 4.1 Integration with Contr ... When two incoming streams present e1 |- P and e2 |- not-P: 1. Contr sets KnowledgeStatus(P) = Contradictory (B={T,F} in FDE). 2. It prevents total logical explosion by trapping the assertion within an isolated contradiction frame. 3. It initializes ResolutionStatus(P) = Unresolved. 4. If d in R_req were collapsed, Contr would either trigger classical explosion or falsely collapse the state into Unknown.
rows.statement: Specifies the required integration between R_req and the Contr contradiction-isolation subsystem: on conflicting evidence e1|-P and e2|-not-P, Contr must set KnowledgeStatus(P)=Contradictory, trap the assertion in an isolated frame to prevent explosion, and initialize ResolutionStatus(P)=Unresolved; explicitly states that collapsing any of D-1.1/D-3.1/D-4.1 would force either classical explosion or a false collapse into Unknown.
invariants: Contr must not classically explode or falsely collapse a contradiction into Unknown

rows.anchor: Architectural Specification: ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Interface (ABK-CONTR-INT-v1) ... The Contr Isolation Module operates directly on top of the Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) to handle non-explosion, contradiction trap frames, and resolution state tracking for paraconsistent evaluations. ... When an inbound assertion or lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu(phi)=B), the ABK-1 engine delegates contradiction containment to ABKContrBridge.
rows.statement: Specifies a bridge architecture (SPEC-ABK-CONTR-2026-V1) between ABK-1 and a Contr contradiction-isolation engine: whenever an ABK-1 lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu=B), the engine delegates containment to an ABKContrBridge that traps the state in a local frame, sets ResolutionStatus=Unresolved, and initializes an evidential polarity edge graph, ensuring downstream inference cannot propagate the contradiction beyond a bounded contextual scope.
invariants: contradictory states are trapped and cannot propagate beyond their scope frame without explicit unwrapping

rows.anchor: we already have a critical KnowledgeOS boundary: Satisfiability != Contr because satisfiability is relative to Semantics + Language + ModelClass. Thus: Cons_S(K) iff exists M, M |=_S K could be a candidate formal consistency property. But it must not become: Contr(K) = not Cons_S(K). ... The attached document itself later says Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status. That is actually evidence against identifying Contr with ordinary satisfiability.
rows.statement: Rejects identifying Contr with ordinary model-theoretic satisfiability: Satisfiability != Contr, since satisfiability is relative to Semantics+Language+ModelClass; proposes Cons_S(K) iff exists M: M|=_S K as a candidate formal consistency property distinct from Contr(K)=not-Cons_S(K), citing the source document's own admission that Contr requires Support Status and Resolution Status as evidence against the satisfiability identification, and listing Contr's broader required distinctions (genuine contradiction, incompatible contexts, temporal divergence, supersession, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness).

rows.anchor: there are still four things we must NOT pretend are solved: A. R_req itself ... Framework complete != Set ratified. B. Evaluation semantics ... Eval_c is not closed yet. C. Zero / Contr ... R_req -> Zero/Contr is a useful connection, but not yet a definition. D. delta ... This is the largest remaining formal gap ... we still haven't established the actual delta signature, preconditions, postconditions, partiality and composition.
rows.statement: Names four things explicitly NOT solved despite the R_req reconstruction: (A) R_req itself -- the framework exists but the final authoritative ratified set does not (Framework complete != Set ratified; the 47 distinctions are a candidate corpus, not canonical ontology); (B) Evaluation semantics -- Eval_c(K,r,Gamma)->EVal has a better place to sit but is not closed (contradiction, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness, temporal qualification, operational blockage, provenance insufficiency, status, boundary remain unresolved); (C) Zero/Contr -- R_req helps explain but does not define either, and Contr cannot become Contr=not-Cons_S(K); (D) delta -- the largest remaining formal gap, still lacking a signature, preconditions, postconditions, partiality, and composition rule.
missing: R_req's ratified set
closed Eval_c semantics
Zero/Contr formal definitions
delta's full signature

rows.anchor: 5.2 Ratification Commitments: 1. Tier P1 Immutability ... 2. Extension Protocol: Formal test vectors, Tractability proof, 2/3 HPA approval ... 3. Compliance Requirement: All kernel projections must achieve Loss_{R_req}(pi) = 0 for P1 distinctions. 4. Zero Definition: Zero is now formally defined as compliance with R_req. 5. Contr Definition: Contradiction is detected via D-1.1 (Contradictory) and managed via ABK-Contr Bridge.
rows.statement: Issues five formal ratification commitments: (1) Tier P1 distinctions are immutable in future minor revisions; (2) any P2/P3 extension requires test vectors, a tractability proof, and 2/3 HPA approval; (3) all kernel projections must achieve Loss_{R_req}(pi)=0 for P1 distinctions; (4) Zero is NOW FORMALLY DEFINED as compliance with R_req; (5) Contradiction (Contr) is defined as detected via D-1.1 (Contradictory) and managed via the ABK-Contr Bridge. Commitments 4 and 5 assert as ratified exactly the two identifications (Zero=R_req-compliance, Contr=D-1.1-plus-Bridge) that the immediately preceding file in this batch (a critical review) argued should not be adopted without further work.
invariants: Tier P1 distinctions are immutable in v1.x
kernel projections must have Loss_{R_req}=0 on P1

rows.anchor: 4.1 R_req -> Contr: D-1.1 (Contradictory) Detection trigger for isolation; D-3.1 (Evidential Direction) Polarity graph for resolution; D-4.1 (Resolution Status) State machine for contradiction management. 4.2 R_req -> Zero: Zero requires: D-1.1 No Contradictory or Underdetermined states; D-2.1 All propositions Current; D-1.2 All propositions have a Justification Mode; D-3.1 No Dual evidence directions. 4.3 R_req -> Evaluation: Evaluation adequacy requires: D-1.1, D-1.2, D-2.1, D-3.1, D-4.2 must be preserved.
rows.statement: Adds an explicit R_req-to-subsystem integration-usage mapping not spelled out this concretely elsewhere in the batch: for Contr, D-1.1 triggers isolation detection, D-3.1 feeds the polarity graph, D-4.1 drives the contradiction-management state machine; for Zero, four specific conditions are required (no Contradictory/Underdetermined per D-1.1, all-Current per D-2.1, a Justification Mode present per D-1.2 for every proposition, no Dual evidence direction per D-3.1); for Evaluation adequacy, D-1.1/D-1.2/D-2.1/D-3.1/D-4.2 must all be preserved.

rows.anchor: The biggest remaining TODO: Evaluation ... Eval_c(K,r,Gamma) -> EVal. What exactly is the semantic domain of EVal? We already found that a flat {T,F,U} cannot represent all required distinctions. FDE-style positive/negative support improves this, but also does not solve the entire problem. The stronger candidate is something factorized along the lines of: Evaluation = Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance but this remains a candidate, not a ratified KnowledgeOS definition.
rows.statement: Names Evaluation's semantic domain as the biggest remaining TODO the R_req framework does not solve: a flat {T,F,U} cannot represent all required distinctions, and FDE-style two-channel support improves but does not fully solve it; proposes a stronger factorized candidate Evaluation = Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance, explicitly labeled a candidate rather than a ratified definition.

rows.anchor: Contradiction remains open ... Contr != False and Contr != U in the simplistic sense. FDE gives a useful two-channel representation: Eval(p) = (S+(p), S-(p)). But FDE alone still collapses important distinctions. Therefore: Contr remains OPEN and cannot yet be used to select the kernel.
rows.statement: Restates Contr's status: experimentally established Contr!=False and Contr!=U in the simplistic sense, with FDE's two-channel Eval(p)=(S+(p),S-(p)) representation useful but still collapsing important distinctions; concludes Contr remains OPEN and cannot yet be used to select the kernel.

rows.anchor: The proposed Trap Frame is the biggest new assumption ... nu(phi)={T,F} implies Frame_trap(phi). This is elegant operationally, but we have not derived it yet. It introduces several new assumptions: 1. contradiction must be isolated; 2. isolation occurs at the proposition level; 3. the isolation boundary is a frame; 4. propagation is prevented by that frame; 5. resolution status becomes Unresolved; 6. evidence continues accumulating inside the frame. ... TrapFrame = PROPOSED not ESTABLISHED. It should be experimentally tested before becoming kernel machinery.
rows.statement: Identifies six distinct unproven assumptions bundled into the proposed Trap Frame mechanism (contradiction must be isolated; isolation is proposition-level; the isolation boundary is a frame; propagation is prevented by that frame; resolution status becomes Unresolved; evidence continues accumulating inside the frame), none of which follows automatically from the established Contr!=False result; classifies Trap Frame as PROPOSED, not ESTABLISHED, requiring experimental testing before becoming kernel machinery.
missing: experimental tests for each of the six bundled Trap Frame assumptions

rows.anchor: Contr -- this document over-closes it ... we did not establish that contradiction is identical to the FDE both-positive/both-negative state. FDE was only shown to be a useful representation of positive/negative support, not a complete KnowledgeOS contradiction semantics ... Correct status: Contr := detectable conflict condition can be closed. But: Contr = (S+>0 and S->0) should remain candidate, unless the threshold and evidence semantics are separately established.
rows.statement: Rejects SPEC-CONTR's identification of Contr with the specific FDE both-positive/both-negative threshold condition as over-closure: FDE was only ever shown to be a useful representation of positive/negative support, not a complete contradiction semantics, and it still collapses important distinctions. Proposes the narrower closed claim 'Contr := detectable conflict condition' while 'Contr=(S+>0 and S->0)' with its specific threshold/evidence numeric semantics remains a candidate, not established.
missing: separate establishment of the threshold and evidence-weighting semantics

rows.anchor: EVal is NOT yet closed ... Problem 1 -- EVal has collapsed evaluation into standing ... insufficient evidence, theory incomplete, unobservable, underdetermined, epistemically inaccessible can all yield the same low-standing result. We already demonstrated that a flat value domain cannot preserve these distinctions. So: EVal != Standing -> FourState must remain a constitutional distinction.
rows.statement: Identifies that SPEC-EVAL's threshold-based four-state derivation (ACCEPTED/REFUTED/CONTRADICTION/UNDERDETERMINED from S+/S- alone) repeats the exact kind of collapse the programme already rejected: insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness, unobservability, underdetermination, and epistemic inaccessibility can all produce the same low-standing result under this mapping. States as a constitutional distinction that EVal must not be identified with a simple Standing-to-four-state function.
invariants: EVal must not collapse to a flat Standing-to-four-state mapping

rationale_evidence.anchor: **`Contr ≠ Zero`** — invariant `I7` holds, but for an uncomfortable reason: they are different objects *because* contradiction produces closure rather than a gap.
rationale_evidence.statement: Establishes I7 (Contr≠Zero) holds, but for an uncomfortable reason -- they differ because contradiction produces closure rather than a gap, not because Zero adequately captures contradiction; Zero remains a lens and must not become an evaluation value, and nothing in this experiment supports promoting it.

rationale_evidence.anchor: > `[INF]` **If the evaluation outcome is identical across a family, then no function of the outcome alone separates any pair in it. Hence no flat domain — of ANY cardinality — indexed by evaluation outcome is adequate.**
rationale_evidence.statement: States the theorem that makes the structural (not cardinal) obstruction rigorous: since under the strongest candidate A all nine no-determinate-value conditions evaluate to the identical outcome U, no function of the outcome alone can separate any pair among them -- hence no flat domain of any cardinality indexed by evaluation outcome is adequate; of ten candidate fields, exactly reason separates all nine on its own.

rationale_evidence.anchor: | detect `Pos ∧ Neg` | `Represent` `Relate` `Discriminate` |...> ### Protocol kernel designation — **`K2`**... **No step required a power outside the candidate set, so contradiction is a SEMANTIC STATE, not a kernel operator.**
rationale_evidence.statement: Kernel derivability analysis: every step (detecting Pos∧Neg via Represent/Relate/Discriminate, classifying subtype via Discriminate/Qualify, deciding resolution via Challenge/Determine, resolving via Revise/Select) is derivable from the existing candidate power set with no step requiring a new power -- contradiction is a semantic state, not a kernel operator (K2, not K1 since current representation cannot carry the needed distinctions, and not K3 since importance is not irreducibility); explicitly this is a protocol-scale designation, not a KnowledgeOS kernel selection.

rationale_evidence.anchor: > `[EXP]` **`Zero` cannot be defined before evaluation semantics are expressive enough to answer "`U` because *what*?"** The dependency is **`Sat → Zero`**, never the reverse.
rationale_evidence.statement: Retrospectively explains why Zero resisted definition: the old Zero(K,I,EC)⟺Δ=∅ was underspecified because Sat itself was -- when Sat(r)=U one must ask 'U because what?' since U_unobservable is epistemically different from U_not-assessed; the dependency is Sat->Zero, never the reverse, confirmed from two independent directions (this experiment's §8, and KR-CONTR-MODELS §6's saturation finding).

rationale_evidence.anchor: * reason has 10 distinct values over 21 conditions; * it does **not** encode the complete state; * reason alone fails to distinguish the Satisfied/Unsatisfied pair; * therefore the tested representation requires another dimension.
rationale_evidence.statement: Cites the E12 sub-result (reason has 10 distinct values over 21 conditions, does not encode the complete state, and alone fails to distinguish Satisfied/Unsatisfied) as justification for testing Reason-only, Standing-only, and Standing+Reason adequacy separately, rather than merely asserting reason is important -- this matches the later formal result in S2495 §9.1's three-guard test.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **Predecessor:** `KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09` — `E-FDE-5` established that composition and frame qualification are coupled. This experiment tests the coupling directly.
rationale_evidence.statement: Records that KR-COMP-2026-09 was commissioned as a direct test of a coupling (composition and frame qualification) already established by a predecessor experiment KR-CONTR-FDE-2026-09's result E-FDE-5 -- confirming the FDE-inspired implementation proposed in S2496/S2497 was actually executed, though its own write-up is not part of this batch.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **You cannot choose the rule before φ**: the rule ranking changes with φ (2 distinct rankings). **But once `φ ⊇ {time, context}`, three rules tie at 5/5**
rationale_evidence.statement: Confirms and sharpens E-FDE-5: composition and frame qualification are coupled, with the frame as the load-bearing half -- rule ranking depends on phi (2 distinct rankings across the phi settings), but once phi⊇{time,context}, majority/last-wins/intraframe-only are indistinguishable (tie at 5/5); the criteria therefore select a frame qualifier, not a composition rule, inverting the expected shape of the original question ('which composition rule?' becomes 'which frame qualifier?', with the rule reported as still open).

rationale_evidence.anchor: **Why the surviving rules agree:** with a frame qualifier in force, **conflict is detected WITHIN a frame**...A suite that separated the rules would need a witness with genuine conflict in one frame and divergence across others — this one has none, and that is a limitation of the suite, not a result.
rationale_evidence.statement: Explains why the three surviving rules agree: with a frame qualifier active, conflict is detected within a frame and the aggregation rule only governs across-frame behavior; the witness suite places all genuine contradictions inside a single frame so the across-frame policy never gets exercised -- explicitly identified as a limitation of the test suite, not a positive finding that the rules are equivalent in general.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Is `Qualify` an **operation**, or an **epistemic boundary rather than a computable function**? | **not decided.** And `KR-CONTR-EVAL` makes the third option live: the programme has already found one case where an apparent function was really a **boundary** (`reason`) | **OPEN**
rationale_evidence.statement: Whether Qualify is an operation or an epistemic boundary (rather than a computable function) is not decided; KR-CONTR-EVAL is cited as precedent making the 'boundary' option live, since that programme already found one case (reason) where an apparent function was really a boundary.

sources.note: Step 106: the runtime layer of the conformance sequence. Four-representation chain A_I->A_C->A_D->A_R with approximate (not literal) conformance; configuration-is-architecture; logical-vs-physical component identity; runtime architecture graph diffing and Drift!=Violation; runtime evidence freshness and DesiredState-vs-ActualState reconciliation; DeploymentTechnicalSuccess!=RuntimeConformance; architecture-aware observability making DDD bounded contexts operational at incident time (contains one explicit FAIL experiment: no component-to-architecture mapping during an outage); runtime-to-governance/code feedback loops with an explicit non-silent-rewrite promotion discipline; runtime snapshotting for historical/incident reconstruction; TechnicalReality vs OrganizationalIntent; Drift as a first-class object with a 6-state lifecycle and TemporalGovernanceDrift. Extends architecture-conformance-engineering-model and drift-detection-capability.

rows.anchor: Steps 101-105 established the conformance model for architecture, semantics, governance, agents. Step 106 asks: does that architecture survive contact with the actual running system? A_I->A_C->A_D->A_R. Crucial requirement: A_R approx A_I subject to explicitly documented runtime differences.
rows.statement: Frames Step 106's central test: whether the architecture survives contact with the running system, via A_I(intended)->A_C(implementation)->A_D(deployed)->A_R(runtime), requiring approximate conformance A_R≈A_I subject to documented differences.

rows.anchor: 106.1 — Why runtime is the final authority for runtime facts ... Documentation ≠ RuntimeEvidence.
rows.statement: States Documentation ≠ RuntimeEvidence: runtime is the final authority for runtime facts, illustrated by a documented ServiceA→ServiceB call diverging from actual production topology.

rows.anchor: 106.2 — Four representations ... Architecture model A_I, Source model A_C, Deployment model A_D, Runtime model A_R. The goal is not necessarily literal equality. It is Conformance(A_I,A_C,A_D,A_R).
rows.statement: Defines the four representations (Architecture/Source/Deployment/Runtime models) and states the goal is Conformance(A_I,A_C,A_D,A_R), not literal equality.

rows.anchor: 106.3 — Experiment 1: deployed version mismatch ... Architecture says KnowledgeOS=2.1. Deployment runs KnowledgeOS=2.0. Expected: DeploymentDrift. Result: PASS. The system must report the mismatch rather than silently assuming the latest code is running.
rows.statement: Experiment 1: a deployed version (2.0) lagging the architecture-declared version (2.1) is DeploymentDrift, which must be reported not silently assumed away; result PASS.

rows.anchor: 106.4 — Experiment 2: configuration mismatch ... Repository defines FeatureX=True. Production configuration FeatureX=False. Expected: runtime behavior must be evaluated using the actual configuration. Result: PASS
rows.statement: Experiment 2: runtime behavior must be evaluated using the actual production configuration (FeatureX=False), not the repository default; result PASS.
