rows.anchor: AAG=(V,E) ... V=V_C∪V_K∪V_I∪V_E∪V_T∪V_F
rows.statement: Defines the Architecture Assurance Graph AAG=(V,E) with node types V_C (components/bounded contexts), V_K (contracts), V_I (invariants), V_E (enforcement mechanisms), V_T (verification tests), V_F (evidence/artifacts), and typed edges Component-owns->Invariant, Contract-carries->SemanticProperty, Mechanism-enforces->Invariant, Test-verifies->Invariant, Evidence-supports->Test/Claim.

rows.anchor: I -> Owner -> Mechanism -> Test -> Evidence
rows.statement: For a critical property I, the complete assurance chain is I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence; a missing edge is potentially an assurance gap. Worked example: I_Authority->Governance->AuthorizationPolicy->NegativeTest->TestEvidence is a complete chain.

rows.anchor: A — Defined and enforced ... D — Claimed but unverifiable
rows.statement: Every invariant is classified into one of four situations: (A) defined and enforced and verified; (B) defined but not enforced (M=empty); (C) implemented but not architecturally declared (a mechanism exists but nobody established which invariant it protects); (D) claimed but unverifiable (documentation asserts I=True but no evidence exists). D is flagged as particularly dangerous.

rows.anchor: Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I) ... Gap(I) in {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical}
rows.statement: Defines assurance gap conceptually as Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I), explicitly refusing to assign arbitrary numerical values and instead classifying into {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} 'until we establish a justified scoring model'.

rows.anchor: Component correctness =/=> System correctness
rows.statement: An architecture may have every individual bounded context (Evidence, Assessment, Governance) correct while still having a critical global assurance gap, e.g. if the contract Assessment->Governance silently drops uncertainty; boxed conclusion: component correctness does not imply system correctness.

lineage_claims.target: earlier corpus assurance-dimension work (step170 broken-chain taxonomy)
lineage_claims.quote: Connection to our earlier work ... Mathematics provides: State + Transition + Constraints.

rows.anchor: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}
rows.statement: States a weakest-link property: for a critical end-to-end property I_global, assurance is bounded by the minimum assurance of its constituent links, explicitly qualified as 'not a universal mathematical law; it is a useful conservative assurance model' — if one indispensable boundary lacks a provenance guarantee, end-to-end provenance cannot be honestly claimed.

rows.anchor: Traceability_syntactic=True but Traceability_historical=False
rows.statement: Decision traceability example D->A->E: traceability is only True if each reference (Decision->Assessment ID->Evidence ID) remains resolvable and semantically versioned; if the Assessment ID resolves only to the latest Assessment, syntactic traceability can hold while historical traceability fails — 'this distinction is crucial'.

rows.anchor: SyntacticCorrectness =/= SemanticCorrectness ... HTTP 200 ... JSON schema valid
rows.statement: Establishes SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness: an HTTP 200 proves transport success but not BusinessMeaningCorrect; a valid JSON schema does not prove SemanticContractValid.

lineage_claims.quote: Our current architecture suggests six dimensions

rows.anchor: A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g)
rows.statement: Proposes a candidate six-dimension KnowledgeOS assurance vector A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g): A_s structural (component exists, boundary explicit, dependencies controlled, contracts defined), A_m semantic (meaning preserved, no overloaded concept, no Boolean replacing a richer state), A_e epistemic/statistical (evidence, inference, assumptions, uncertainty, correlation vs causation, model version), A_t temporal (which version/policy/model applied when, historical reconstructability), A_p provenance (claim origin, traversable chain), A_g governance (who was authorized, under which valid policy, permission vs execution).

rows.anchor: Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization
rows.statement: Argues a single global assurance score is dangerous: if A_s=1 but A_p=0, a scalar like 0.83 could falsely imply reasonable assurance, whereas for critical systems one missing indispensable property may be enough to block certification; boxed principle: vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization — an explicit statistical-design principle.

rows.anchor: C0 — Informational ... C4 — Critical assurance
rows.statement: Provisionally classifies invariant criticality into five levels: C0 Informational (documentation/style), C1 Functional (normal business behavior), C2 Semantic (meaning/context preservation), C3 Governance (authority/policy/compliance), C4 Critical assurance (safety, irreversible action, high-impact decision, legally significant state); flagged as needing later validation against real KnowledgeOS use cases.

rows.anchor: Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I))
rows.statement: Proposes assurance-mechanism selection as a function of criticality: low-risk -> Documentation+UnitTest; medium -> IntegrationTest+ContractTest; high -> PropertyBasedTest+Replay+AuditEvidence; critical -> FormalModel/Proof where practical — self-labeled 'a proposed framework, not yet a frozen standard'.

rows.anchor: A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance)
rows.statement: Proposes an AI-generated-artifact metadata schema A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance), stating the schema must be derived from the actual KnowledgeOS implementation but conceptually AI output should not be treated as an unexplained opaque fact.

lineage_claims.quote: CandidateArtifact =/= AuthoritativeArtifact

rows.anchor: AI -> CandidateResult -> DeterministicValidation -> AcceptedArtifact. Not: AI -> ProductionTruth
rows.statement: States the architecture must route AI output through AI->CandidateResult->DeterministicValidation->AcceptedArtifact, never directly AI->ProductionTruth, calling this distinction 'central to our KnowledgeOS design'.

rows.anchor: TrustedFor(x,p,t) ... Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose)
rows.statement: Warns against another bare Boolean (`trusted = true`); trust/assurance must be contextual, TrustedFor(x,p,t) — an artifact trustworthy for Task_1 need not be trustworthy for Task_2. Generalizes to Valid(x) being usually incomplete; the better form is Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose), called 'a major insight for KnowledgeOS': validity is not absolute but ValidForPurpose(P).

rows.anchor: StructuralValid ... SemanticValid ... EpistemicallyValid ... TemporallyValid ... GovernanceValid
rows.statement: Distinguishes five validity types (Structural/Semantic/Epistemic/Temporal/Governance Valid), concluding Valid(x) should be treated as shorthand only when the intended dimension is explicitly known.

rows.anchor: Different missing edges represent different classes of architectural weakness
rows.statement: States the missing-node principle: Invariant->Owner with no Enforcement is a design gap; Enforcement->Test missing is an assurance gap; Test->Evidence missing is an auditability gap — different missing edges are different classes of architectural weakness, letting the architecture 'diagnose itself' via forall I_i: Complete(AAG(I_i))? producing a reproducible gap report.

rows.anchor: System -> Output + EvidenceOfCorrectness
rows.statement: Reframes the architecture's strongest form as System->Output+EvidenceOfCorrectness rather than merely System->Output, stated as precisely what deterministic assurance is trying to accomplish.

rows.anchor: We should not claim: 'The architecture is mathematically proven.' ... FormalizableArchitecture
rows.statement: Explicit self-warning: the architecture must not be claimed as mathematically proven; what exists is a FormalizableArchitecture, and the next task is determining which portions can actually be Formalized->Specified->Verified.

rows.anchor: ### DDD ... VERY STRONG ... Gītā 1–4 ... DEEP CONSISTENCY
rows.statement: Step 211 verdict: DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, and AI are each rated VERY STRONG, and Gita chapters 1-4 rated DEEP CONSISTENCY, citing continued distinctions Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Action, Capability!=Authority, PastState!=CurrentState, Decision!=Outcome.

lineage_claims.quote: This will be our next major step.

rows.anchor: Implemented | Partially Implemented | Specified Only | Missing | Unknown ... Unknown =/=> Implemented
rows.statement: Previews Step 212 (Architecture Gap Discovery): every derived invariant must be classified as Implemented / Partially Implemented / Specified Only / Missing / Unknown, with an explicit warning not to infer Unknown=>Implemented; names the goal of producing a 'KnowledgeOS Architecture Assurance Gap Register' covering 14 listed areas (identity, versioning, provenance, temporal validity, epistemic status, uncertainty, contradiction, authority, decision/action separation, execution/outcome separation, AI validation, deterministic assurance, contract semantics, state transitions).

lineage_claims.quote: We can extend the AAG

rows.anchor: Assessment -/-> Authority ... The X is important. It represents a path that the architecture must prevent
rows.statement: Extends the Step 211 Architecture Assurance Graph with an explicit forbidden-path marker: Evidence->Assessment->Governance->Decision->Authorized Action->Execution->Outcome, with an explicit forbidden edge Assessment-/->Authority that the architecture must prevent.

lineage_claims.quote: We can now extend the Architecture Assurance Graph into

rows.anchor: EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) ... Invariant -> Test -> Evidence. This creates a closed assurance loop
rows.statement: Extends the Architecture Assurance Graph into an Evidence-Architecture-Graph EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) with edges Evidence->Claim->Decision->Architecture->Invariant and potentially Invariant->Test->Evidence, closing the assurance loop, then generalizes to the full cycle Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge, calling architecture 'a learning system'.

rows.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
rows.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

rows.anchor: Independent arithmetic verification of Step 211's 0.83 illustration
rows.statement: Independent arithmetic check (executed via python3) of Step 211 Section 211.17's illustration A_s=1, A_p=0, aggregate 0.83 over 6 assurance dimensions under an unweighted mean: the maximum attainable mean with A_p=0 is 5/6 = 0.8333, so the illustrated 0.83 requires the other four dimensions to average 0.995 -- i.e. it sits at 99.6% of the theoretical maximum. The arithmetic is not wrong (0.83 is attainable) but the example is a near-degenerate corner case rather than a representative aggregate (a more representative figure would be (1+0+0.8x4)/6 = 0.70); as a warning the rhetoric holds, but as an illustration of a plausible aggregate it is unrepresentative. No repair asserted.

rows.anchor: LATER RESPONSE IN SCOPE: Step 211 reverses Test/Evidence order; Step 212 drops the Owner column and recalibrates E_n
rows.statement: Step 210 cites only Step 209 by number ('up to Step 209, we have asked...'). Later response: Step 211 Section 211.2 restates the assurance chain with Test before Evidence, contradicting Step 210's own Section 210.40; Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15 minus the Owner column; Step 212 Section 212.6 re-mints an E_0..E_5 scale with different rung definitions than Step 210 Section 210.30's E_1..E_5.

rows.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: AAG=(V,E); Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I); Component correctness !=> System correctness; A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g)
rows.statement: Step 211 ('Architecture Assurance Graph') is the only in-scope file with a .md extension. It models assurance as a typed graph AAG=(V,E), V=V_C∪V_K∪V_I∪V_E∪V_T∪V_F (components/contracts/invariants/enforcement/tests/evidence); boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence and Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I) with Gap(I) in {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical}; boxes 'Component correctness ⇏ System correctness'; states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; distinguishes Traceability_syntactic from Traceability_historical, boxing 'SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness'; boxes a 6-dimension assurance vector A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g) and 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization'; introduces criticality classes C0-C4, Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I)), an AI-artifact 7-tuple, AuthorityLevel(x) in {Candidate,Validated,Governed,Authorized,Executed}, and Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose).

rows.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY (cited BY NUMBER). ZERO — the only file in the band that cites no prior step by number at all
rows.statement: Step 211 opens by referring to 'the Invariant Verification Matrix' by title, not number, and its Section 211.32 ('Connection to our earlier work') names six disciplines (DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, AI engineering, the Gita lens) and zero steps. Later response in scope: Step 212 Section 212.30 extends the AAG diagram with a forbidden edge (Assessment -X-> Authority); Step 213 Section 213.33 extends it to EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture).

rows.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES, UNRESOLVED; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR with an arity mismatch against Step 210's own preview
rows.statement: Step 211 turns the matrix into a graph and poses the diagnostic question for-all I_i: Complete(AAG(I_i))?, answered for zero of the 15 invariants. CLEAR: situations A/B/C/D, the missing-edge taxonomy (design/assurance/auditability gap), Traceability_syntactic vs Traceability_historical, TrustedFor(x,p,t). Arity mismatch: Step 210's tail previewed AAG=(Components,Contracts,Invariants,Evidence,Dependencies), a 5-tuple, but Step 211 delivers AAG=(V,E) with 6 node classes (Enforcement and Tests are new; Dependencies is gone) -- the preview and the delivery share only three of five/six components.

rows.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 211.6's min{Assurance(...)} is ill-typed against Section 211.17's own vector-assurance boxed rule
rows.statement: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1), Assurance(I_2), ...} (Section 211.6) requires a total order on Assurance's codomain, but the same file declares gaps to be ordinal categories (Section 211.4), assurance to be a 6-vector (Section 211.9), and explicitly forbids the scalarization that would make min well-defined (Section 211.17, boxed: 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization'). Min over a 6-vector is undefined without a scalarization the file itself forbids -- the two boxed positions are in direct conflict (Contradiction #6); everything conditioned on the weakest-link model is conditional on repairing this. Secondary: Section 211.17's own numbers (A_s=1, A_p=0, aggregate 0.83) are cardinal values on dimensions Section 211.4 declared ordinal -- independently computed as sitting at 99.6% of the space's ceiling, correct arithmetic but an unrepresentative illustration.

rows.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: zero graph nodes, zero edges, zero classifications produced; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
rows.statement: AAG=(V,E) is DEFINED but no instance is constructed (not INPUTS_KNOWN, no node is ever named); Complete(AAG(I_i)) is DEFINED but evaluated for 0 of 15 invariants; Gap(I) is DEFINED but assigned to 0 invariants; A=(A_s..A_g) is DEFINED but computed for 0 artifacts; min{Assurance(...)} is ILL-TYPED, not even DEFINED; Criticality(I)/C0-C4 is DEFINED but assigned to 0 invariants; Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I)) gives f as a 4-row informal lookup, never applied. Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED -- the file is one level of abstraction above tests, no tests specified.

rows.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: VERY STRONG on design principle (vector over premature scalarization), WEAK on execution (both violated in the same file); MEASUREMENT VERDICT: the band's clearest scale-type failure
rows.statement: Section 211.17's refusal of a scalar assurance aggregate (a single indispensable zero can be masked by a high mean) is correct and a real, well-known aggregation pathology, and Section 211.4's refusal to assign numbers to gaps ('more honest until we establish a justified scoring model') is right -- but the file then uses min (Section 211.6) and cardinal 0/1/0.83 values (Section 211.17), the two operations its own principle forbids, in the same file. Measurement table: Gap(I) ordinal, unused -- justified; A_s..A_g vector scale unstated, then assigned cardinal 1/0 -- unjustified; Assurance(I) forbidden to scalarize, then min{...} applied requiring total order -- unjustified; the aggregate 0.83 requires ratio/interval scale the file itself rejects -- unjustified (though self-aware, quoted to be rejected); Criticality(I) ordinal C0-C4 used correctly as an argument to f -- justified; AuthorityLevel(x) 5 states used correctly, with the file itself correctly warning it may need to be several independent dimensions rather than one.

rows.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG (Component correctness !=> System correctness; SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness; CandidateArtifact != AuthoritativeArtifact); UL: three overlapping five/six-fold taxonomies of the same space never cross-mapped
rows.statement: Section 211.5's Component correctness ⇏ System correctness is the correct DDD statement of the composition problem (the fifth boxing of the 048/058/208.13 proposition in the corpus, still uncited each time); Section 211.8's SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness with concrete HTTP-200/JSON-schema-valid examples is well chosen; Section 211.23's CandidateArtifact != AuthoritativeArtifact is genuinely useful for AI-in-the-loop domains; Section 211.26's contextual validity Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose) is correctly argued. Deficiency: the AAG is never instantiated against Step 206's contexts or Step 205's aggregates, so no DDD artifact is actually assured. UL: Section 211.27's five kinds of validity (Structural/Semantic/Epistemic/Temporal/Governance) is excellent discipline ('Valid(x) should be treated as shorthand only when the intended dimension is explicitly known'), but is near-isomorphic to, yet not identical with, the six assurance dimensions (A_s..A_g) and the C0-C4 criticality classes introduced 40 lines apart -- three overlapping taxonomies of one space, zero cross-mappings.

rows.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS; WHAT SURVIVES / DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 211
rows.statement: Stated: assurance is monotone in its weakest link; six dimensions suffice; criticality determines mechanism. Hidden: that the six assurance dimensions are independent (required for the vector to be informative; A_p and A_t are plainly coupled by the file's own example); that RequiredAssurance(I) is externally given (Gap(I)=Required-Actual has an undefined minuend); that a 'missing edge' is discoverable (presupposes the graph already exists; it does not). Survives: the four situations A/B/C/D, the missing-edge taxonomy, Component correctness ⇏ System correctness, SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness, Traceability_syntactic vs historical, vector-assurance-over-scalarization as a principle, Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose), CandidateArtifact != AuthoritativeArtifact, and Section 211.33's 'we should not claim: the architecture is mathematically proven. Not yet' (the most honest sentence in the band). Does not survive: min{Assurance(...)}; the cardinal A_s=1,A_p=0,0.83 illustration; the AAG as an object (zero instances); any one of the three overlapping taxonomies as *the* taxonomy.

single_candidate_flags.why_uncertain: Independently re-derives the idea that epistemic state should be split into orthogonal dimensions (here: Acquisition mode, Support, Resolution, Validity) rather than one combined enum -- structurally the same corrective move as the pre-existing multi-dimensional-epistemic-state-model object (B0012's EpistemicStanding/EvidenceCondition/OperationalDisposition split), though with different named dimensions; genuinely unclear whether this is the same recurring insight or an independent parallel discovery given no citation between them.

Fully worked answer to Question 4A: a five-dimensional Sigma=(Acquisition,Support,Resolution,Validity,Conflict) vector with a combinatorial 2240-state space, each dimension enumerated with values and Zero/Lord/Sarathi question tables. Same uncertainty as the S0776 entry regarding relation to the pre-existing multi-dimensional-epistemic-state-model object (B0012).
Standalone republication of the same 5-dimensional epistemic state model already recorded under S0778; same relation-to-existing uncertainty as that entry.

sources.note: Self-correction of an earlier single combined state list (UNKNOWN/ABSENT/INSUFFICIENT/QUESTIONABLE/CONFLICTED/REJECTED/VALIDATED): splits it into separate dimensions -- EpistemicStanding (SUPPORTED/NOT_PROVEN/CONFLICTED/REJECTED/UNKNOWN), EvidenceCondition (ABSENT/INSUFFICIENT/ADEQUATE/CONTESTED/INVALID), OperationalDisposition (NO_ACTION/INVESTIGATE/PROCEED/BLOCK/ESCALATE) -- to avoid a combinatorial single state machine.

rows.anchor: the opposite of belief is not necessarily disbelief; the proper opposite can be conscious ignorance or doubt. Deliberate doubt can amount to a 'not proven' verdict because the evidence does not determine either side. ... NOT_PROVEN != REJECTED.
rows.statement: Whately's doubt-is-not-disbelief distinction motivates preserving BELIEF/DISBELIEF/DOUBT/IGNORANCE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE as potentially distinct states and adding a NOT_PROVEN state distinct from REJECTED to the epistemic-state model.

rows.anchor: DDD says we should separate dimensions. ... Claim: EpistemicStanding, EvidenceCondition, AuthorityStanding, OperationalDisposition. ... Otherwise we create a combinatorial state machine.
rows.statement: Self-correction of the previously proposed single combined epistemic-state list into four independent Claim-attached dimensions (EpistemicStanding, EvidenceCondition, AuthorityStanding, OperationalDisposition), avoiding a combinatorial single state machine.

lineage_claims.target: the earlier single combined epistemic-state list (UNKNOWN/ABSENT/INSUFFICIENT/QUESTIONABLE/CONFLICTED/REJECTED/VALIDATED)
lineage_claims.quote: I would now not make all of those one state machine. DDD says we should separate dimensions.

rows.anchor: UNKNOWN does not necessarily mean: Nobody knows. It can mean: The current inquiry has not established an epistemically sufficient standing for this proposition. ... UNKNOWN_TO_US while KNOWN_BY_SOURCE_A or KNOWN_IN_CONTEXT_B.
rows.statement: Refines UNKNOWN to mean 'the current inquiry has not established sufficient epistemic standing', distinct from 'nobody knows'; proposes UNKNOWN_TO_US as compatible with KNOWN_BY_SOURCE_A or KNOWN_IN_CONTEXT_B, connecting back to Russell's acquaintance/description distinction and Davidson on interpretation.

rows.anchor: CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) \subseteq Preserved(P_t)
rows.statement: Presentation is loss-aware: as a projection it may lose information but must not lose epistemically important distinctions — e.g. Observed/Reported/Inferred/Assumed must not all collapse into 'FACT', and Strong/Weak/No evidence must not all collapse into 'CONFIDENT'. Defines EpistemicFidelity(P_t,S_t) and requires CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) ⊆ Preserved(P_t) as one of the most important invariants of the presentation architecture.

rows.anchor: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(\Sigma)
rows.statement: Recommends removing 'Confidence' (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None) as the primary presentation model because it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state established in Q16 (Acquisition ≠ Support ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Validity). A table example shows presenting each claim's Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity separately; a UI may then derive a simplified indicator: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(Σ), not Confidence = Σ.

lineage_claims.target: this document's own Confidence Indicators section 5.1
lineage_claims.quote: This is useful for UI, but it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state we established in Q16.

rows.anchor: Support \neq Probability
rows.statement: Extends the earlier Q16 correction (Support ≠ Truth, Support ≠ Resolution) with Support ≠ Probability unless a probabilistic model is explicitly defined — 'Strong evidence' does not mathematically mean P(True)=0.95 unless the system has actually defined that probability semantics.

lineage_claims.target: Q16 correction establishing Support ≠ Truth and Support ≠ Resolution
lineage_claims.quote: Our Q16 correction was excellent. Keep: Support \neq Truth ... But add: Support \neq Probability

rows.anchor: UncertaintyType \neq UncertaintyMagnitude
rows.statement: Uncertainty vocabulary (None/Low/Moderate/High/VeryHigh) is acceptable as a policy vocabulary but not yet a mathematical quantity — the theory has not decided whether uncertainty means lack of information, ambiguity, variance between sources, probability, confidence, or epistemic indeterminacy; flags UncertaintyType ≠ UncertaintyMagnitude as a future question.
missing: formal probabilistic/epistemic semantics of uncertainty

rows.anchor: StrongSupport \not\Rightarrow Current
rows.statement: Validity should be separated into TemporalValidity(A,t) and EpistemicStatus(A): a fact can be strongly supported but temporally expired, so StrongSupport ⇏ Current.

rows.anchor: Evidence = (Source,\ Content,\ Relevance,\ Reliability,\ Time,\ Provenance)
rows.statement: Evidence needs its own model rather than being just 'E': Evidence = (Source, Content, Relevance, Reliability, Time, Provenance), plus an EvidenceRelation(A,E) since evidence may support, weaken, contradict, qualify, or contextualize an assertion. Establishes Evidence ≠ Support — Support is a relation/assessment between evidence and assertion, called 'a significant missing DDD object'.

rows.anchor: HierarchyOfFaculties \neq EpistemicConfidence
rows.statement: Chapter 3 (verses 40, 43) orders Senses<Mind<Intelligence<Self as distinct faculties, tempting an 'epistemic ladder' reading; explicitly rejects that reading (reaffirming the earlier rejection of Unknown<Observed<Confirmed<Resolved as a universal ladder): HierarchyOfFaculties ≠ EpistemicConfidence — the text describes different faculties/levels of operation, not better evidence. Abstracts a non-theological CognitiveCapability = {Perception, Interpretation, Reasoning, Judgment, Orientation}, explicitly kept out of Σ_A and placed in the actor/agent model instead.

rows.anchor: Knowledge \neq Understanding
rows.statement: Called 'perhaps the most important validation of the entire KnowledgeOS concept': a person can act on FalseInterpretation while possessing many correct facts (Arjuna's opening situation), giving Knowledge ≠ Understanding and CorrectFacts ⇏ CorrectDecision. Formally defines Understanding U=(ConceptualModel,Relations,Implications,NormativeMeaning,DecisionConsequences,Uncertainty): Knowledge = 'what is represented', Understanding = 'what does it mean, imply and require in this context'.

rows.anchor: Understanding = Interpretation of relationships among known propositions in context
rows.statement: Confirms K≠U (Knowledge ≠ Understanding, validated by Arjuna's opening bewilderment despite already having heard distinctions) but corrects the previous U=(ConceptualModel,Relations,Implications,NormativeMeaning,DecisionConsequences,Uncertainty) tuple as too implementation-oriented; redefines Understanding as 'interpretation of relationships among known propositions in context', from which implications, consequences, applicability and normative significance are derived facets.

lineage_claims.quote: That is useful, but too implementation-oriented for the ontology.

rows.anchor: Gītā hierarchy \neq KnowledgeOS epistemic hierarchy
rows.statement: Names 'perhaps the most important correction': the Senses<Mind<Intelligence<Self hierarchy (verses 40,43) is a metaphysical faculty hierarchy from the source, not evidence for an Observation<Interpretation<Reasoning<Truth epistemic-confidence ladder — that would be 'our invention, not the text'. Similarly the smoke/dust/embryo covering analogy should not become a software confidence scale; the only legitimate architectural extraction is 'AccessToKnowledgeCanBeObscuredToDifferentDegrees', with the exact ontology left to the source's own philosophical model.

lineage_claims.target: S0807's use of the Senses<Mind<Intelligence<Self ordering as support for a CognitiveCapability faculty model
lineage_claims.quote: I previously interpreted this as evidence for a "faculty/capability model." That is reasonable as an analogy, but we must not turn it into: Observation < Interpretation < Reasoning < Truth. That would be our invention, not the text.

rows.anchor:
Information 
eq Evidence 
eq Belief 
eq Knowledge 
eq Understanding
rows.statement: Endorses the book's knowledge/understanding distinction (understanding requires coherent explanatory grasp) and extends the research lattice to a five-term chain Information ≠ Evidence ≠ Belief ≠ Knowledge ≠ Understanding, explicitly flagged as 'a research distinction, not yet a Core object model'. Evaluates the book summary's proposed relation set (observes, measures, knows, understands, complements, constitutes, limits) one by one, rejecting 'constitutes(measurement,knowledge)' as too theory-laden to become a Kernel relation until measurement is shown universally necessary.

rows.anchor: U_{sem}\neq U_{epi}\neq U_{dom}
rows.statement: Rejects InterpretationConfidence=EpistemicSupport (an LLM can be extremely confident in an incorrect interpretation) and introduces three distinct uncertainties: Semantic uncertainty U_sem (what does the source mean?), Epistemic uncertainty U_epi (how well supported is the proposition?), Domain uncertainty U_dom (what is actually true in the domain?) — U_sem≠U_epi≠U_dom, 'a significant strengthening of our earlier four-dimensional epistemic model'. Also states Ambiguity ≠ Error: multiple candidate meanings (e.g. 'Nexus is running' as OperationalStatus/Process/NexusService running) should be preserved until context resolves them — ambiguity is itself a valid epistemic state.

rows.anchor: Unknown ... Hypothesized ... Reported ... WeaklySupported ... ModeratelySupported ... StronglySupported ... Confirmed ... Conflicting ... Stale ... Invalidated ... Absent
rows.statement: Expands the epistemic state space Σ into an eleven-value enumeration with worked examples: Unknown (dimension exists, value unknown), Hypothesized (candidate proposed, unevaluated), Reported (source reported, unverified), WeaklySupported, ModeratelySupported, StronglySupported, Confirmed (verified via multiple independent sources), Conflicting (multiple sources disagree), Stale (once known, may no longer be current), Invalidated (believed then disproven), Absent (determined not to exist). Defines the Admission Boundary formally: Admit:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->Assertion, explicitly NOT requiring StronglySupported, Confirmed, or Truth — 'admission means this proposition is now part of the Knowledge State, with an explicit epistemic status', a much lower and more defensible boundary than a truth-threshold.

type_signature.domain: candidate assertion x evidence x rules x context

rows.anchor: Support = f(E,\Pi,C,\mathcal R)
rows.statement: Rejects Support=|E| (evidence count) since evidence differs in relevance, reliability, independence, freshness, provenance, directness, context: Support=f(E,Π,C,R). Requires an explicit evidence-dependency graph to detect non-independent evidence — e.g. if Document->LLM (the LLM derived its answer from the document), the LLM's output is not independent evidence even though it appears as a fourth source alongside DB/Monitoring/Document — 'evidence independence must be explicitly modelled', flagged as important for Zero.

Evidence ≠ EvidenceQuality: even a poor-quality observation-proposition pair can be an evidence relation; quality is evaluated separately as a 7-dimensional vector Q_E=(Reliability,Relevance,Directness,Independence,Freshness,Reproducibility,ProvenanceQuality) rather than a single confidence number — 'much more faithful than confidence=0.87'. EvidenceType≠EvidenceStrength (a direct measurement can be wrong; a mathematical derivation can be extremely strong; an official document can be stale), and EvidenceQuality=f(E,P,C,R) since e.g. a direct runtime observation may dominate for 'what is running now?' while an official architecture document may dominate for 'what was officially approved?' — no universal ranking exists.

rows.anchor: E_1 \succeq_{P,C,R} E_2
rows.statement: Rejects a universal total ordering E_1>E_2 in favor of a partial comparison E_1≽_{P,C,R}E_2 ('under proposition P, context C and rule R, E_1 is at least as suitable as E_2'), since evidence can be genuinely incomparable (e.g. a direct runtime measurement vs an official governance decision). Evidence quality vectors are compared via a policy ComparisonRule(P,C)->Ordering rather than collapsed to a scalar average (e.g. Q(E_1)=(0.95,0.98,1.0,...) is NOT reduced to Q(E)=0.94) — different policies weight different dimensions (directness/freshness for runtime state; authority/provenance for governance compliance).

type_signature.domain: evidence pairs x proposition x context x rule

rows.anchor: Reliability(E) = f(Source, ObservationMethod, Environment, Configuration, Context, Provenance)
rows.statement: Corrects Reliability from a property of the source alone to Reliability=f(Source,ObservationMethod,Environment,Configuration,Context,Provenance): even an 'official Nexus database' can produce an unreliable observation if queried against the wrong environment, a stale replica, or a broken synchronization. Corrects Completeness similarly to be proposition-relative — Completeness(E,P,C,ρ), not Completeness(E) — since a version field alone may be complete for 'what is the version?' but radically incomplete for 'is Nexus ready for migration?'.

rows.anchor: IndependenceFactor(ER, evidence_graph) = 1 / (1 + dependency_depth(ER, evidence_graph))
rows.statement: Delivers concrete computable Layer-2 functions for Evidence Assessment: WeightedStrength(ER,policy,context)=reliability(ER)×relevance(ER)×currency(ER)×independence_factor(ER,evidence_graph); IndependenceFactor(ER,G)=1/(1+dependency_depth(ER,G)) (worked example: direct DB evidence depth 0 -> independence 1.0; an LLM citing that DB depth 1 -> independence 0.5; an LLM merely trained on it depth 2 -> independence 0.33); AggregateSupport(evidence_set,policy)=sum(WeightedStrength(ER_i))/(1+log(count(evidence_set))) — logarithmic dampening 'prevents linear scaling with the number of evidence items'; ConflictStatus derived from support/contradict levels crossing a threshold (Active/Potential/None).

rows.anchor: DeriveEpistemicState(assessment, policy, context) → Sigma
rows.statement: Gives a worked, example-deterministic default rule for DeriveEpistemicState(assessment,policy,context)->Σ: VeryStrong support + no conflict -> Confirmed; VeryStrong support + potential conflict -> StronglySupported; >=Moderate support + no conflict -> ModeratelySupported; >=Weak support + no conflict -> WeaklySupported; >=Weak support + active conflict -> Conflicting; no support + no contradiction -> Unknown; substantial contradiction -> Contradicted; otherwise Reported. Explicitly policy-dependent: AssessEvidence(ρ1)≠AssessEvidence(ρ2) for the same evidence set. Fourteen EVD invariants (EVD_1..14) frozen, adding EVD_13 (assessment functions must be auditable) and EVD_14 (all assessment results must be reproducible from provenance) to the eleven from S0847.

rows.anchor: Quality \neq Score
rows.statement: Corrects the quality vector Q(e)=(q_R,q_Re,q_F,q_I,q_C) to use CATEGORICAL domains (Q_R={Unknown,Low,Medium,High}) rather than numbers initially, with numeric mapping deferred to policy: Quality ≠ Score — 'this protects the theory from prematurely committing to numerical confidence'.

rows.anchor: A(E)=\max_i s_i ... A(E)=\sum_i s_i ... A(E)= \frac{\sum_i w_i s_i}{\sum_i w_i}
rows.statement: Three simple aggregation candidates are each rejected/downgraded with a specific counterexample against the 10-case test universe (proposition P: Nexus.version=3.69): Candidate A Max(s_i) — rejected because A({e_1})=A({e_1,e_3}), ignoring independent corroboration entirely; Candidate B Arithmetic sum Σs_i — rejected because repeating the same evidence e_1 unboundedly grows A(E), violating Duplicate Invariance and enabling evidence spam; Candidate C Weighted average — insufficient because two equal-strength independent observations (s(e_1)=s(e_2)=0.9) still yield A=0.9, so corroboration does not necessarily increase the assessment.

rows.anchor: 1-\prod_i(1-s_i)
rows.statement: Candidate D, the saturating combination A(E)=1-∏(1-s_i) used in the prior experiment (S0850), gives desirable bounded, corroboration-increasing behavior (two independent 0.8-strength items combine to 0.96) but carries a hidden semantic assumption — that each s_i behaves like an independent probability of successfully supporting the proposition — which is not universally justified for non-probabilistic evidence-strength dimensions: mathematically valid as an operator, but 'candidate, not constitutional'.

rows.anchor: P(H\mid E) = \frac{P(E\mid H)P(H)}{P(E)}
rows.statement: Candidate E Bayesian evidence P(H|E)=P(E|H)P(H)/P(E) is mathematically rigorous but requires P(H) and P(E|H) that are 'often not objectively available' for arbitrary documents/testimony, so it should be an optional inference policy, not the foundational evidence model. Candidate F Dempster-Shafer (Bel(P), Pl(P)) maps well onto Support≠Truth (permits unresolved uncertainty rather than forcing one probability) but introduces its own calculus/combination rules, so it too is 'a useful pluggable reasoning mechanism', not a mandatory core. Candidate G pure ordinal reasoning (Low<Moderate<Strong<VeryStrong, no arithmetic) avoids pretending 'Strong' equals a number like 0.8 — 'excellent core representation' — but cannot naturally express fine-grained aggregation alone.

rows.anchor: Ordering\neq Combination\neq Inference
rows.statement: Distinguishes three mathematically different operations that were being conflated: Ordering e_1≽e_2 ('at least as suitable under policy ρ'), Combination e_1⊕_ρe_2 ('combine their contributions'), Inference Γ⊢_ρP ('the inference rule derives P') — Ordering≠Combination≠Inference, 'a major refinement'. Proposes a KnowledgeOS Core Evidence Calculus (Evidence, Proposition, Polarity, Provenance, Dependency, Quality dimensions, Context, Assessment, Conflict) as fixed/constitutional, with a pluggable Inference Algebra layer (OrdinalPolicy, WeightedPolicy, BayesianPolicy, StatisticalPolicy, DempsterShaferPolicy, RulePolicy) — analogous to DDD's Evidence bounded context (owns Evidence and its invariants) vs Reasoning bounded context (owns InferenceRule and its mathematical semantics), 'prevents the KnowledgeOS kernel from becoming a giant AI confidence calculator'.

rows.anchor: a\oplus a=a
rows.statement: Defines algebraic requirements for any aggregation operator ⊕: closure, commutativity (evidence arrival order should not change the final assessment), associativity (enables streaming/incremental updates without full recomputation), an identity element 0_E ('no additional evidential contribution'), and idempotence a⊕a=a for duplicate evidence — but explicitly notes idempotence must NOT be required for genuinely independent corroboration (otherwise e_1⊕e_2 would behave like e_1⊕e_1 and corroboration would be lost); idempotence therefore applies to evidential-equivalence/dependency CLASSES, not raw evidence objects.
invariants: a ⊕ a = a (for equivalence classes only)

rows.anchor: \mathcal E/{\sim}
rows.statement: Introduces the equivalence class [e] of evidence that should not be independently counted (e_1∼e_2 if they represent the same underlying evidential contribution, so [e_1]=[e_2] and only one contribution is counted, while [e_1]≠[e_3] for genuinely independent e_3), giving aggregation a mathematical foundation over the quotient ℰ/∼ rather than raw ℰ — 'a significant result' resolving the idempotence-vs-corroboration tension. Revised pipeline: ℰ --Normalize--> ℰ/∼ --AssessQuality--> Q --⊕_ρ--> EA --Inference_ρ--> Conclusion.

rows.anchor: There is no universal scalar evidence algebra for KnowledgeOS.
rows.statement: States a provisional theorem: there is no universal scalar evidence algebra for KnowledgeOS, because the requirements combine fundamentally different semantics (ordinal quality, dependency, contradiction, context, policy, probabilistic uncertainty, logical entailment) that a single scalar cannot preserve without information loss — therefore 'Structured Evidence Assessment is fundamental' and 'Scalar Evidence Score is a policy-specific projection', called 'one of the strongest mathematical principles in the whole KnowledgeOS theory'. Proposes an eleven-property algebraic test table (duplicate invariance, commutativity, associativity, identity, boundedness, corroboration, dependency-awareness, contradiction preservation, context sensitivity, policy sensitivity, reproducibility) and recommends implementing four candidate algebras side-by-side (Max, weighted mean, saturating 1-∏(1-s_i), Bayesian) tested automatically against all twelve laws as the next experiment.
invariants: There is no universal scalar evidence algebra for KnowledgeOS

rows.anchor: We do not choose mathematics because it looks useful. We test candidate mathematics against the semantics and invariants of KnowledgeOS.
rows.statement: Adopts an explicit triple-role methodology (senior mathematician: algebraic structure/invariants/proof obligations/counterexamples; senior statistician: uncertainty/dependence/sampling/calibration/likelihood/robustness; senior DDD architect: bounded contexts/aggregates/policies/events/implementation boundaries) governed by the rule: mathematics is chosen only if it passes tests against KnowledgeOS's own semantics and invariants, never merely because it 'looks useful'.

rows.anchor: \text{Probability}\neq\text{Confidence Score}
rows.statement: Introduces Calibration as a new statistical test property: if a system claims P(H)=0.9, then among all cases classified at approximately 0.9, roughly 90% should actually satisfy H, or the number '0.9' is merely a number pretending to be a probability — Probability≠Confidence Score, one reason not to casually convert KnowledgeOS's epistemic states into probabilities. Separately warns that Bayesian conditional-independence P(E_1,E_2|H)=P(E_1|H)P(E_2|H) is violated by an evidence CHAIN (Database->LLM->Report->Human presentation, i.e. E_1->E_2->E_3->E_4, not four independent observations); treating chained evidence as independent 'can produce severe overconfidence' — validating the dependency graph as a first-class KnowledgeOS concept.

rows.anchor: | Max           |                  ✅ |             ❌ |                  possible |             ❌ |                      ❌ |
rows.statement: Pre-registers a hypothesis table (explicitly marked hypothesis, not conclusion, 'we should let the experiment establish the result') predicting per-candidate pass/fail across Duplicate/Corroboration/Dependency/Contradiction/Probability-semantics: Max passes duplicate invariance but fails corroboration/contradiction/probability semantics; Weighted mean is problematic on duplicate, weak on corroboration; Saturating passes duplicate (marked with caveat) and corroboration, handles dependency only with preprocessing, partial contradiction handling, probability semantics only under assumptions; Bayesian passes corroboration and probability semantics 'with correct model', requires an explicit dependency model, 'can' handle contradiction. Proposes ten adversarial test cases for the next experiment: 100 copies of the same document; 100 LLMs reading the same document; 10 genuinely independent measurements; 5 contradictory authoritative sources; stale+current evidence; highly reliable but irrelevant evidence; weak but independent evidence; evidence chains; missing provenance; deliberately misleading evidence — to produce a 'KnowledgeOS Evidence Calculus Test Report' with Pass/Fail/Conditional verdicts per law, determining what belongs in the kernel vs a policy vs an optional statistical mechanism.

experiment.hypothesis: Max, Weighted Mean, Saturating combination, and Bayesian Updating will each satisfy a different subset of the duplicate/corroboration/dependency/contradiction/probability-semantics properties, none satisfying all.
experiment.setup: Same normalized 10+ case evidence universe as prior experiments, extended with ten adversarial cases.
experiment.assumptions: n/a (this is a pre-registration, not yet run)
experiment.inputs: Ten adversarial evidence scenarios listed in the statement.
experiment.method: Run all four candidate algebras against the full property/law checklist and tabulate pass/fail/conditional.
experiment.limitations: This document only pre-registers the hypothesis; the actual experiment and its results are not contained in this file.

rows.anchor: No simple scalar operator is sufficient as the KnowledgeOS epistemic foundation.
rows.statement: Reports the executed property-test results (CSV artifact) for four candidate evidence-combination operators across seven properties: MAX passes duplicate-invariance/dependency-awareness/order-invariance/staleness/boundedness but FAILS independent corroboration; Weighted Mean FAILS duplicate invariance, corroboration, and dependency-awareness; Saturating and Bayesian-like both pass all seven (irrelevance-handling is attributed to the separate normalization/quality layer, not the raw operator). Conclusion: no simple scalar operator is sufficient as the KnowledgeOS epistemic foundation — confirming the earlier theorem from S0851.

lineage_claims.target: S0852's pre-registered hypothesis table for the four candidate algebras
lineage_claims.quote: We have now completed the first adversarial property test.

experiment.hypothesis: MAX, Weighted Mean, Saturating, and Bayesian-like aggregation operators will differ in which of seven epistemic-integrity properties they satisfy.
experiment.setup: Adversarial evidence sets including ~100 duplicate copies of one document, multiple LLM outputs derived from a single source, and contradictory authoritative sources, run through each of the four candidate operators.
experiment.assumptions: The Bayesian-like candidate used a 'toy likelihood mapping' explicitly flagged as unsuitable for the constitution.
experiment.inputs: Adversarial evidence universe described in S0852 plus ~100 duplicate-document and multi-LLM cases.
experiment.method: Apply each candidate operator and score against duplicate invariance, independent corroboration, dependency-awareness, irrelevance handling, order invariance, stale-evidence retention, and boundedness.
experiment.result: MAX and Weighted Mean each fail at least one core property (corroboration for both; duplicate invariance and dependency-awareness additionally for Weighted Mean); Saturating and Bayesian-like pass all seven tested properties.
experiment.interpretation: Confirms that no simple scalar operator alone can serve as the KnowledgeOS epistemic foundation; a dependency-normalization layer must precede any scalar aggregation.
experiment.limitations: Bayesian-like result relied on a toy likelihood model, not a defensible dependence model; full quantitative results are only in the external CSV, not reproduced in-document.
experiment.conclusion: Freeze a Kernel (Evidence/Provenance/Dependency/Polarity/Context/TemporalValidity/QualityDimensions/Conflict/StructuredAssessment) vs Policy (Aggregation/Inference/DecisionThreshold/RiskTolerance/EvidenceAdequacy) architectural split, and treat evidence-identity/equivalence as the next unresolved research problem.

rows.anchor: 100\times\text{same evidence} \not\Rightarrow 100\times\text{knowledge}
rows.statement: Confirms EvidenceCount≠IndependentEvidenceCount with a worked dependency-graph example (one API observation branching to two LLM interpretations is 1 underlying observation + 2 derived representations, not 3 pieces of evidence) and e∼e' ⇒ Contribution([e])=Contribution([e']): ~100 generated duplicate copies of the same evidence produce essentially the same evidential contribution as the single original observation — 100×same evidence ⇏ 100×knowledge, called 'one of the most important anti-hallucination/anti-amplification properties of the architecture'. Multiple LLM outputs derived from one source (e_2=LLM(e_1), e_3=LLM_2(e_1)) are confirmed non-independent (e_2⊥̸e_1, e_3⊥̸e_1) and cannot be treated as three independent confirmations — giving KnowledgeOS the capability (absent from ordinary RAG systems) to 'distinguish information propagation from independent corroboration'.

rows.anchor: BayesianInference \neq EvidenceScore
rows.statement: Cautions that the Bayesian-like candidate's apparent success in the experiment used a deliberately 'toy likelihood mapping' not suitable for the KnowledgeOS constitution — genuine Bayesian inference requires P(H), P(E|H), and a defensible dependence model, none of which are generally available: BayesianInference ≠ EvidenceScore; BayesianInference ∈ KnowledgeOS Reasoning Policies (a pluggable policy, never kernel content).

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel\n\nThe kernel should define: Evidence, Provenance, Dependency, Polarity, Context, TemporalValidity, QualityDimensions, Conflict, StructuredAssessment
rows.statement: Freezes the Kernel/Policy separation reached through this experimental arc: KnowledgeOS Kernel defines Evidence, Provenance, Dependency, Polarity, Context, TemporalValidity, QualityDimensions, Conflict, StructuredAssessment; the Policy layer defines Aggregation, Inference, DecisionThreshold, RiskTolerance, EvidenceAdequacy, so different domains can adopt different reasoning policies without corrupting the epistemic kernel. Aggregation pipeline: ℰ --N(normalize)--> ℰ/∼ --Q(quality)--> Q --ρ(policy)--> EA --I_ρ(inference)--> Conclusion.

rows.anchor: Unknown\ Dependency\neq Independence
rows.statement: Identifies the single remaining unresolved mathematical problem: the equivalence relation e_1∼e_2 ('epistemic equivalence') itself is not yet formally defined — e.g. are 'Nexus is version 3.69' (Document A) and 'Nexus 3.69 is installed' (Document B) duplicates, independent corroboration, two observations from the same source, or semantically equivalent but independently acquired? Names the needed research object: an 'Evidence Identity and Dependency Calculus'. States the crucial default-safety principle: Unknown Dependency ≠ Independence — if KnowledgeOS cannot establish that two sources are independent, it must NOT silently assume independence, called potentially 'one of the strongest foundations of the entire evidence architecture'. Final honest status: Evidence representation/Conflict preservation/Dependency awareness rated 'strong'; Aggregation theory 'deliberately open'; Evidence identity/equivalence 'still needs formalization' — closing with the methodological stance 'do not patch the gap with another definition; isolate it, construct counterexamples, and formalize the missing relation.'
missing: formal definition of the epistemic-equivalence relation ∼

rows.anchor: The inverted tree ... Omega -> knowledge structure -> K_1,K_2,K_3,... But we must not turn this into an ontology automatically. It is a structural metaphor ... many knowledge states can exist within a larger knowledge space ... a useful visualization rather than proof of a graph ontology. ... Epistemic quality = f(K,M,B,Gamma,evidence,provenance) ... fits extremely well with our existing multi-dimensional epistemic-state work ... Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity/Provenance
rows.statement: Chapter 15's inverted tree gives Omega -> knowledge structure -> K_1,K_2,K_3,... as a structural metaphor (many knowledge states can exist within a larger knowledge space), explicitly warned not to be turned into an automatic ontology -- a visualization, not proof of a graph ontology. Chapters 16-18 add that knowledge is not evaluated only by what it contains but by how it is held/processed/acted upon, giving Epistemic quality = f(K,M,B,Gamma,evidence,provenance), said to fit extremely well with the pre-existing multi-dimensional epistemic-state work (Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity/Provenance) rather than a single scalar confidence.

lexical.anchor: the opposite of belief is not necessarily disbelief; the proper opposite can be conscious ignorance or doubt. Deliberate doubt can amount to a 'not proven' verdict because the evidence does not determine either side. ... NOT_PROVEN != REJECTED.

conceptual.anchor: UNKNOWN does not necessarily mean: Nobody knows. It can mean: The current inquiry has not established an epistemically sufficient standing for this proposition. ... UNKNOWN_TO_US while KNOWN_BY_SOURCE_A or KNOWN_IN_CONTEXT_B.

formal.anchor: DDD says we should separate dimensions. ... Claim: EpistemicStanding, EvidenceCondition, AuthorityStanding, OperationalDisposition. ... Otherwise we create a combinatorial state machine.

rationale_evidence.anchor: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(\Sigma)
rationale_evidence.statement: Recommends removing 'Confidence' (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None) as the primary presentation model because it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state established in Q16 (Acquisition ≠ Support ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Validity). A table example shows presenting each claim's Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity separately; a UI may then derive a simplified indicator: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(Σ), not Confidence = Σ.
