sources.note: S0890's Step 25A.5: attacks each of I1-I10 (all PASS conceptually), discovers two genuine counterexample threats (circular derivation, evidence identity) plus three further threats (recomputation cost, stale rule/model/ontology versioning, temporal authority), promotes I11-I14 as new invariants, refines K to (V,E,R,T,P,D,M), explicitly discloses automated execution has NOT yet been run (conceptual falsification only), delivers a 17-row status table and a CONDITIONAL PASS verdict for the whole 25A phase; hands off to Step 25B (adversarial end-to-end Nexus-migration simulation).

rows.anchor: We now move from constructing examples to trying to break the model. This is the point where I want to be particularly strict as a mathematician/statistician: a model is not validated because we can construct cases that work. We need to search for counterexamples.
rows.statement: Announces the shift to actively searching for counterexamples rather than constructing more confirming examples — a model is not validated merely because working cases can be built.

rows.anchor: Objective ... K_{t+1}=T(K_t,e_t) with the candidate invariants I_1,\ldots,I_{10}. The question is: \exists e_1,\ldots,e_n such that I_j(K_n)=False? If yes, we have found a counterexample. That counterexample tells us which part of the theory must be refined. ... What we are going to generate ... E=\
rows.statement: Frames the falsification objective ∃e1,...,en: Ij(Kn)=False as the search criterion, and specifies a seven-kind evidence generator and nine-kind event generator whose ordering matters.

rows.anchor: Invariant I1 — Historical immutability ... Create K_1. Create K_2. Retract evidence from K_2. Inspect K_1. Expected K_1^{after}=K_1^{before}. Conceptually PASS. The snapshot architecture supports this naturally. ... Invariant I2 — Explicit revision ... Try to modify an assertion without generating a
rows.statement: Attacks I1 (historical immutability, PASS) and I2 (explicit revision, requiring the NoSilentMutation DDD invariant to reject unmoderated assertion mutation).

rows.anchor: Invariant I3 — Provenance ... Create A_{fake}: BackupVerified=True with Support(A_{fake})=\varnothing. Attempt Commit(A_{fake}). Expected Commit=False. PASS conceptually. This is one of the strongest properties of the model. ... Invariant I4 — Explicit conflict ... A_1: Version=3.69 and A_2: Version
rows.statement: Attacks I3 (provenance, PASS, one of the strongest model properties) and I4 (explicit conflict, PASS, requiring both assertions retained plus a Conflict object).

rows.anchor: Invariant I5 — Temporal validity ... A_1 valid [t_0,t_1] and A_2 valid [t_2,t_3] with t_1<t_2. Naive implementation would produce Conflict=True. Correct implementation Conflict=False. PASS conceptually, but this exposes an implementation requirement: Conflict detection must evaluate temporal overlap
rows.statement: Attacks I5 (temporal validity, PASS, exposing the requirement that conflict detection must evaluate temporal overlap) and I6 (preserve Unknown, PASS, essential).

rows.anchor: Invariant I7 — Dependency propagation ... E_1\rightarrow A_1, A_1\rightarrow A_2, A_2\rightarrow Decision. Invalidate(E_1). Expected impact propagates through the chain. The model supports the requirement. But here we discover a significant unresolved issue: What happens if the dependency graph cont
rows.statement: Attacks I7 (dependency propagation, model supports the chain requirement) but discovers a significant unresolved issue: cyclic dependency graphs are not yet formally handled.

rows.anchor: Counterexample candidate #1 — Circular derivation ... A_1\vdash A_2 and A_2\vdash A_1. A naive dependency propagation algorithm could recurse forever. CircularDependency is a real computational threat. New requirement: The derivation graph must either prohibit cycles; explicitly represent strongly c
rows.statement: Identifies a genuine counterexample: circular derivation (A1⊢A2⊢A1) could cause infinite recursion in a naive propagation algorithm, proposing (PROPOSED, not established) an AcyclicDerivationGraph constraint for the kernel initially, deferring circular fixed-point semantics.

rows.anchor: Invariant I8 — AI boundary ... LLMOutput: "Rollback verified." with no source. Attempt Commit. Expected Commit=False. Now provide a real document from which the LLM extracts the same assertion. Expected Commit may become possible because the underlying evidence exists, not because the LLM said it. P
rows.statement: Attacks I8 (AI boundary, PASS, distinguishing unsupported hallucination from legitimate extraction) and I9 (replayability, PASS for deterministic operations, revealing the AI-nondeterminism issue next).

rows.anchor: AI and nondeterminism ... Extract(Document). Run 1: A_1. Run 2: A_2. The outputs may differ. Therefore the system cannot rely on LLM(Document) being deterministic. Instead we need to record LLMExecution=(model,version,prompt,context,input,output,time). Then the epistemic record remains reproducible
rows.statement: Discovers LLM extraction is inherently nondeterministic (two runs may differ), requiring an LLMExecution=(model,version,prompt,context,input,output,time) record so the epistemic event remains reproducible even though the underlying AI process is not.

rows.anchor: Invariant I10 — Idempotency ... Register(E) twice. State(Register(E,E)) = State(Register(E)). Otherwise duplicated ingestion could artificially increase evidence. PASS conceptually, assuming stable evidence identity. But that phrase exposes another unresolved problem: How do we determine evidence id
rows.statement: Attacks I10 (idempotency, PASS conceptually) but flags the assumption of stable evidence identity as itself an unresolved problem.

rows.anchor: Counterexample candidate #2 — Evidence identity ... Document A: "Nexus version 3.69" and Document B: "Nexus version is 3.69." Are these SameEvidence? Not necessarily. They may be independent; copied; semantically equivalent; derived from the same system; completely unrelated. Therefore EvidenceIdent
rows.statement: Identifies a second genuine counterexample: two textually-similar documents are not automatically the same evidence (five distinct possible relationships), so EvidenceIdentity cannot simply be Hash(Text) — deferred to a later identity-resolution problem.

rows.anchor: Invariant I11 — No hindsight ... this wasn't in the original ten, but the experiment shows it deserves promotion. KnowledgeBasis(D_t)=K_t. Not K_{current}. Attack: Change current knowledge dramatically. Recalculate historical decision. Expected D_t remains unchanged. PASS conceptually.
rows.statement: Promotes a new invariant I11 (no hindsight): KnowledgeBasis(D_t)=K_t, never K_current, attacked and PASSing conceptually.

rows.anchor: Invariant I12 — World/knowledge independence ... Generate WorldEvent(W_t\rightarrow W_{t+1}) without an observation. Then K_t=K_{t+1}. This must be allowed. Conversely K_t\rightarrow K_{t+1} may occur while W_t=W_{t+1}. This must also be allowed. PASS conceptually. This is one of the foundational pr
rows.statement: Promotes invariant I12 (world/knowledge independence, both directions), attacked and PASSing conceptually, called one of the foundational properties of the architecture.

rows.anchor: Invariant I13 — Revision must not imply falsehood ... A=True then invalidate its only evidence. Correct result: A=Unknown. Not A=False. PASS conceptually. This is especially important for statistical reasoning. ... Invariant I14 — Conflict resolution must preserve history ... Resolution chooses A_2.
rows.statement: Promotes invariants I13 (revision must not imply falsehood — Known→Unknown not →False) and I14 (conflict resolution preserves history via Superseded status), both attacked and PASSing conceptually.

rows.anchor: Now we have discovered two genuine threats ... Threat 1 CircularDependencies. Threat 2 EvidenceIdentity. Both can cause incorrect computation if implemented naively. This is exactly what we wanted from 25A.5.
rows.statement: Consolidates the two genuine unresolved threats found (CircularDependencies, EvidenceIdentity), explicitly the intended outcome of the falsification exercise.

rows.anchor: A third threat appears ... A_1\rightarrow A_2\rightarrow A_3\rightarrow A_4 ... with thousands or millions of derived assertions. A single invalidation can cause O(N+M) recomputation. Therefore KnowledgeOS may eventually require dependency indexes; incremental recomputation; cached assessments; affe
rows.statement: Identifies a third threat: at scale, invalidation-driven recomputation could reach O(N+M), requiring eventual indexes/incremental recomputation/caching/subgraph calculation, while deliberately deprioritizing optimization until correctness is established.

rows.anchor: Fourth threat — stale rules ... A_1 was derived under RuleVersion=r_1. Later RuleVersion=r_2. If we recompute A_1, we may obtain a different result. Therefore provenance must eventually include not just evidence, but RuleVersion and potentially ModelVersion. This is extremely important. Knowledge is
rows.statement: Identifies a fourth threat: recomputing a derived assertion under a later rule version can produce a different result, requiring RuleVersion and ModelVersion be part of provenance — knowledge is derived under a computational context.

rows.anchor: Fifth threat — changing ontology ... an assertion was interpreted using ontology version O_1. Later O_2 changes the meaning of an entity or relationship. Then old derived knowledge may need reassessment. Ontology is not merely static metadata. It can become part of epistemic lineage.
rows.statement: Identifies a fifth threat: ontology version changes can require reassessing old derived knowledge, meaning ontology is part of epistemic lineage, not static metadata.

rows.anchor: Sixth threat — source authority changes ... E_1 was supported by an authoritative source. Later that source loses authority. Does the evidence become false? No. But its current applicability may change. Truth\neq Authority and Authority(t) may itself be temporal. This suggests Authority needs tempor
rows.statement: Identifies a sixth threat: a source losing authority does not falsify its prior evidence but changes current applicability, requiring temporal semantics for Authority itself.

rows.anchor: Falsification summary ... Surviving principles: WorldState\neq KnowledgeState, HistoricalKnowledgeImmutable, Unknown preserved, Conflict explicit, LLMOutput\neq Knowledge, Provenance required, TemporalValidity required, Revision explicit, Replayability required, Decision history protected. ... Newly
rows.statement: Consolidates ten surviving principles and six newly discovered requirements (EvidenceIdentity, DependencyCycleHandling, RuleVersionLineage, ModelVersionLineage, OntologyVersionLineage, TemporalAuthority) exposed by the falsification exercise, not yet elevated to bounded contexts.

rows.anchor: Important mathematical insight ... KnowledgeOS knowledge is not simply K=\{A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_n\}. It is closer to K=(V,E,R,T,P,D,M) where V=epistemic objects; E=evidence/support relations; R=assessments/rules; T=temporal semantics; P=provenance; D=dependency/derivation; M=model/ontology/rule versions
rows.statement: Refines KnowledgeState to K=(V,E,R,T,P,D,M) — epistemic objects, evidence/support, assessments/rules, temporal semantics, provenance, dependency/derivation, model/ontology/rule versions — marked STRONG EMERGING ARCHITECTURAL RESULT (not final), summarized as 'KnowledgeOS is increasingly revealing itself as a governed temporal epistemic graph'.

rows.anchor: Is 25A now complete? Not quite. We have performed the logical falsification design and identified counterexamples, but there is an important distinction: We have not yet executed thousands of randomized transitions in an actual program in this response. Therefore I will not falsely label this as a c
rows.statement: Explicitly discloses that automated randomized property-based execution has NOT been run in this session; only conceptual/formal adversarial falsification has been completed, a distinction preserved for scientific integrity.

rows.anchor: Overall Step 25A Verdict ... Minimal state Viable. Evidence pipeline Viable. Assessment Viable, mathematics incomplete. Assertion lifecycle Viable. Temporal state Viable. Conflict representation Viable. Revision Viable, algebra incomplete. Retraction Viable, dependency algorithm incomplete. Provenan
rows.statement: Delivers a seventeen-row overall status table for Steps 25A.1-25A.5, marking most components Viable (some with incomplete mathematics) and three genuinely Unresolved plus one New requirement.

rows.anchor: My senior conclusion ... 25A — CONDITIONAL PASS. Why not simply "PASS"? Because we have discovered genuine unresolved mathematical/computational questions. Why not "FAIL"? Because none of the foundational distinctions has been shown to be internally impossible. The important outcome is: The model su
rows.statement: Verdicts overall Step 25A as CONDITIONAL PASS, explicitly justified as neither PASS (genuine open questions remain) nor FAIL (no foundational distinction shown internally impossible) — the model survives the first attack while its missing mathematics becomes visible, called exactly what a good research model should do.

rows.anchor: What this means for KnowledgeOS ... KnowledgeOS Kernel = Temporal + Provenance + Evidence + Assessment + Assertion + Revision + Dependency with Unknown and Conflict as first-class epistemic states, not errors. And above that foundation: EpistemicContract \rightarrow Sufficiency \rightarrow Zero \rig
rows.statement: Consolidates the emerging kernel definition (Temporal+Provenance+Evidence+Assessment+Assertion+Revision+Dependency, with Unknown and Conflict as first-class states) and the layer above it (EpistemicContract→Sufficiency→Zero→Lord→Sārathi) as a significant architectural boundary.

rows.anchor: Therefore I recommend Step 25B ... Step 25B — Adversarial End-to-End KnowledgeOS Simulation. Here we will take the Nexus migration problem and construct a complete simulated KnowledgeOS case. It will include Documents + Database + Internet + HumanInstruction + Rules + Constitution + ADR + LLMOutput
rows.statement: Proposes Step 25B: a complete adversarial end-to-end Nexus-migration simulation over eight heterogeneous input kinds through the full ten-stage pipeline including Zero/Lord/Sārathi/Governance, with six categories of deliberately injected problems, to finally test the whole KnowledgeOS concept (not just its knowledge-state kernel) end-to-end.

sources.note: Book chapter IV.4's ratified content: the prose registry of all twelve open questions ratified as open-by-ruling (not by neglect), each with its own closing act named (OQ-1 eta-totality; OQ-2 kernel membership; OQ-3 aggregation operator; OQ-4 action semantics; OQ-5 unexecuted EG-05 suites; OQ-6 Omega-b record gap; OQ-7 the Lord name; OQ-8 Atma-Kernel; OQ-9 the v1.1 lane; OQ-10 constitution banner; OQ-11 EKS relationship; OQ-12 the missing ordering sentence), plus a closing taxonomy pairing them into six two-item classes (mathematical, formal-semantic, executional, historical-record, naming, relational).

rows.anchor: 1 open-by-ruling status [R]; 2 twelve entries verbatim-faithful to FA-6 [U/E]; 3 closing acts named per entry [E]; 4 taxonomy reading [IN marked]. **No OQ resolved, softened, or ranked by preference.**
rows.statement: Chapter IV.4's four claims: the twelve items are open by explicit ruling [R]; each entry is verbatim-faithful to the FA-6 register [U/E]; each entry names its own closing act [E]; and the six-pair taxonomy is marked interpretation [IN]. Explicit constraint: no open question is resolved, softened, or ranked by preference in this chapter.

rows.anchor: Twelve questions are open in the ratified architecture — open **by ruling**, not by neglect. The ratifying act said it in so many words: their unresolved status *is part of the ratified architecture* and must not be treated as accidental incompleteness or silently resolved downstream.
rows.statement: Framing ruling: the twelve open questions are open by explicit ratifying act, not by neglect; their unresolved status is itself part of the ratified architecture and must never be treated as accidental incompleteness or silently resolved downstream.

rows.anchor: **OQ-1 · η-totality.** Does the goal retain any residual role inside the gap function, or do the contract-derivation η capture everything? No evidence either way; the ruled signature is the conservative one; a formal synthesis of η, or evidence of a residual consumer, would close it.
rows.statement: OQ-1 (eta-totality): whether the goal retains any residual role inside the gap function or the contract-derivation eta captures everything entirely; no evidence either way, the ratified signature is deliberately the conservative one; closed by a formal synthesis of eta or evidence of a residual consumer.

rows.anchor: **OQ-2 · Kernel membership.** Which formal objects are irreducible? The traditions are layered (III.9); the membership act — an irreducibility analysis or a formal-side selection ruling — has never happened.
rows.statement: OQ-2 (kernel membership): which formal objects are irreducible remains unsettled; the three kernel traditions are layered (III.9) rather than adjudicated, and no irreducibility analysis or formal-side selection ruling has ever occurred.

rows.anchor: **OQ-3 · The aggregation operator.** The one genuine experiment ended in a principled negative; two candidates survived; none was selected. A successor experiment designed dependency-first would close it.
rows.statement: OQ-3 (the aggregation operator): the sole genuine experiment (EXP-01) ended in a principled negative result; two candidate operators survived but none was selected; a successor experiment designed dependency-first would close it.

rows.anchor: **OQ-4 · Action semantics.** The boundary between knowing and doing is firm; what an authorized action formally *is* — its effects, its failures, its attribution — is specified only in parts.
rows.statement: OQ-4 (action semantics): although the boundary between knowing and doing is firm, what an authorized action formally is -- its effects, its failure modes, its attribution -- is specified only partially.

rows.anchor: **OQ-5 · The unexecuted suites.** Formal test suites exist as specifications (EG-05). Running them is the whole remaining act.
rows.statement: OQ-5 (unexecuted suites): formal test suites already exist as specifications (EG-05); the entire remaining act needed to close this question is to run them.

rows.anchor: **OQ-6 · The Ω-b record gap.** Unboundedness was dropped by disuse, never by act. A one-line historical annotation would close the record; the annotation is HELD.
rows.statement: OQ-6 (the Omega-b record gap): the unboundedness property was dropped by disuse rather than by any explicit act; a one-line historical annotation would close the record, but that annotation is currently HELD (not executed).

rows.anchor: **OQ-7 · The Lord name.** Two historical referents, never reconciled; a terminology ruling — book-relevant, architecture-open.
rows.statement: OQ-7 (the Lord name): two distinct historical referents for 'Lord' were never reconciled; a terminology ruling would close this book-relevant but architecture-open question.

rows.anchor: **OQ-8 · Ātma-Kernel.** A complete hypothesis arc without a disposition act; held as an unresolved lens by explicit decision (D-FA-5); an adoption or rejection act would close it either way.
rows.statement: OQ-8 (Atma-Kernel): a complete hypothesis arc left without any disposition act, held as an unresolved lens by explicit ruling D-FA-5; either an adoption or a rejection act would close it.

rows.anchor: **OQ-9 · The v1.1 lane.** Intake deferred pending a dedicated conformance pass (IV.3).
rows.statement: OQ-9 (the v1.1 lane): intake of the Reference Architecture v1.1 branch is deferred pending a dedicated conformance pass, per chapter IV.3.

rows.anchor: **OQ-10 · The constitution banner.** The ratification act is real; the document's banner is stale; the one-line synchronization is HELD.
rows.statement: OQ-10 (the constitution banner): the underlying ratification act is real, but the constitution document's status banner is stale; the one-line synchronization fix is HELD, not executed.

rows.anchor: **OQ-11 · EKS.** The oldest question in the record: what is KnowledgeOS *to* the engineering knowledge system it grew beside? A scoping act would close it.
rows.statement: OQ-11 (EKS): the oldest question in the whole record -- what KnowledgeOS is to the Engineering Knowledge System it grew up beside -- would be closed by a commissioned scoping act.

rows.anchor: **OQ-12 · The missing ordering sentence.** Dependency-first (I-6) is TESTED in the model and stated nowhere in the repository. One sentence, in the right governed place, would close it.
rows.statement: OQ-12 (the missing ordering sentence): invariant I-6 (dependency-first) is TESTED in the formal model but stated nowhere in the repository; one sentence, placed in the right governed location, would close it.

The programme's last lesson is that an architecture which ca

sources.note: Step 126's opening problem: deriving the first-class semantic objects of KnowledgeOS and the relationships making the control loop traversable.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeObject + Evidence + Decision + Authority + Observation + Finding + Action + Verification
rows.statement: Opens Step 126 (KnowledgeOS Information Model): having defined constitutional rules, evidence, governance, actors, authority, decisions, observations, findings, actions, verification, and feedback conceptually, the next step must derive the semantic first-class objects (KnowledgeObject, Evidence, Decision, Authority, Observation, Finding, Action, Verification) and their relationships, posing the key question 'what are the actual first-class objects of KnowledgeOS, and which relationships make the entire control loop traversable?'

rows.anchor: K=Knowledge, E=Evidence, D=Decision, A=Authority, O=Observation, F=Finding, X=Action, V=Verification
rows.statement: Poses the first-class object hypothesis (K,E,D,A,O,F,X,V) but argues the architecture depends more on relationships between them than on the nouns; diagrams the minimal control loop Knowledge->ExpectedState->[compare]->Observation->Evidence->Finding->Decision->Authorization->Action->Verification->back to Knowledge as the semantic backbone.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeObject ├── id ... └── relationships
rows.statement: Treats Knowledge as a category (architecture principles, decisions, domain knowledge, implementation rules, governance policies, system facts, configuration expectations, approved exceptions, organizational standards) requiring a KnowledgeObject.type field; gives a candidate KnowledgeObject schema (id, type, subject, content, status, provenance, authority, validity, version, relationships), explicitly conceptual only; requires stable KnowledgeObjectID so references (e.g. Decision->KnowledgeObject) are not textual guesses; distinguishes type from status (an ArchitectureDecision may be Proposed/Approved/Superseded, type≠status) and status from validity (an approved decision may be Approved but not yet CurrentlyEffective); defines provenance (KnowledgeObject -derivedFrom-> Source, with source types document/meeting/decision/repository/system/observation/external regulation/agent analysis) as distinct from authority (KnowledgeObject -authorizedBy-> Authority), preventing Source=Authority — a document can source a claim without being the organizationally binding authority.

rows.anchor: Evidence ├── id ... └── epistemic_status
rows.statement: Defines Evidence as something used to support a claim/finding/verification (not simply 'a document'), with candidate schema (id, type, source, observed_at, produced_by, content/reference, version, hash, epistemic_status) and evidence types SourceEvidence/RuntimeEvidence/TestEvidence/BuildEvidence/HumanEvidence/AgentEvidence, each itself needing provenance (e.g. TestEvidence -producedBy-> Checker; RuntimeEvidence -observedBy-> System); states the fundamental distinction Evidence ≠ Knowledge — evidence supports a proposition while knowledge represents a proposition recognized within the epistemic/governance model (Evidence -> KnowledgeClaim).

rows.anchor: Observation ├── id ... └── evidence
rows.statement: Defines Observation (what was actually observed) with schema (id, subject, observed_state, observed_at, observer, environment, evidence), giving runtime reality a first-class representation; distinguishes Observation ≠ Evidence — an observation is an event/statement about observed state (e.g. 'Container X running') while evidence is the material supporting/recording it (e.g. the runtime API response); also introduces ExpectedState ⊆ Knowledge (e.g. 'Nexus deployment must use image version X') requiring provenance back to KnowledgeObject/Authority so the system can answer 'why is this the expected state.'

rows.anchor: Finding ├── id ... └── governance
rows.statement: Defines Finding (a meaningful discrepancy or condition requiring disposition) with schema (id, type, expected, observed, evidence, classification, severity, status, governance); states Finding ≠ Observation — an observation is A=B while a finding is A=B AND A≠Expected, so Finding = Observation + Interpretation + RuleContext; lists finding classifications Violation/Exception/ExpectedChange/FalsePositive/Unknown, required to remain explicit.

rows.anchor: Decision ├── id ... └── supersedes
rows.statement: Defines Decision (records an authoritative choice) with schema (id, subject, choice, rationale, authority, effective_from, effective_until, evidence, supersedes), calling it one of the most important first-class objects; distinguishes an agent Recommendation from Decision (Recommendation is not automatically Decision) with its own relationships Recommendation -basedOn-> Evidence and -proposedFor-> Decision, preserving the agent's contribution without confusing it with authority.

rows.anchor: Authority ├── actor ... └── valid_until
rows.statement: Defines Authority (actor, role, action_scope, resource_scope, delegation, valid_from, valid_until) letting the system answer 'was this actor authorized to perform this action at this time on this resource'; distinguishes Authority (basis of legitimate power) from Authorization (the actual determination CanActorPerformAction?), formalized as Authorize(Actor,Action,Resource,Context) -> Allow/Denied, potentially deterministic where policy permits.

rows.anchor: Action ├── id ... └── evidence
rows.statement: Defines Action (something actually done) with schema (id, actor, type, target, requested_by, authorized_by, started_at, completed_at, result, evidence); states Decision ≠ Action — a decision says 'do X,' an action says 'X was actually done' — critical for auditability.

rows.anchor: Verification ├── id ... └── evidence
rows.statement: Defines Verification (establishes whether an expected condition holds) with schema (id, rule, subject, input, checker, checker_version, executed_at, result, evidence); states Verification = Observation + Rule (e.g. observation 'deployment is version 5' vs. verification 'version 5 conforms to rule R17').

rows.anchor: derivedFrom, supportedBy, authorizedBy, governs, supersedes, observedBy, producedBy, comparesWith, resultsIn, requires, implementedBy, executedBy, verifiedBy, resolves, updates
rows.statement: Formulates a 15-item relationship vocabulary, argued to be potentially more important than the objects themselves, assembled into a core relationship graph: Authority -authorizes-> Decision -governs-> Expected State -comparedWith-> Observation -supportedBy-> Evidence -> Finding -resolvedBy-> Action -verifiedBy-> Verification -updates-> Knowledge.

rows.anchor: D1 -governs,[t1,t2]-> K.
rows.statement: Argues relationships themselves need temporal validity (D1 governs K only for [t1,t2]; past t2, D1 is no longer the current governing decision); requires supersession (D2 -supersedes-> D1) to be explicit rather than inferred from timestamp ordering alone, since a later-created decision does not necessarily supersede an earlier one semantically.

rows.anchor: Claim -supportedBy-> Evidence; Claim -hasStatus-> Inferred/Verified/Authoritative.
rows.statement: Introduces Claim as a not-yet-modeled object: something the system says is true/false/expected/proposed (e.g. 'Service X owns database Y'), with Claim -supportedBy-> Evidence and -hasStatus-> Inferred/Verified/Authoritative; distinguishes KnowledgeObject as the container/lifecycle object from Claim as its semantic assertion, flagged as important for AI-generated knowledge; worked example Claim C42 progressing INFERRED (with evidence E91/E92 and recommendation R17) -> VERIFIED (on verification PASS) -> AUTHORITATIVE (on governance), yielding the knowledge-lifecycle chain Observation -> Claim -> Evidence -> Verification -> Governance -> Authority, more precise than 'the agent learns.'

rows.anchor: Claim ↛ Authority without the promotion process.
rows.statement: States an agent can produce a Claim, attach Evidence, and request Verification, but Claim cannot become Authority without the promotion process; requires agent-generated objects to carry Producer (e.g. Claim.producedBy=ClaudeSession123) and session provenance (Agent, Session, Prompt/Task, Tools, ToolResults — not necessarily full prompt text, but enough lineage to reconstruct how a result was generated).

rows.anchor: Claim → ToolExecution → RepositoryState.
rows.statement: Defines ToolExecution as first-class evidence (id, agent, session, tool, input_reference, output_reference, execution_time, environment, result) so an agent claim like 'I verified the service dependency' links to the actual tool call and repository state, assembled into a complete AI evidence chain Agent->Task->Tool Execution->Observation->Evidence->Claim->Verification->Governance, argued to be substantially stronger than storing only the agent's final text.

rows.anchor: Semantic Governance Ledger
rows.statement: Proposes the analogy 'KnowledgeOS as Semantic Governance Ledger' (not a financial ledger, but sharing immutability/traceability requirements) since it records what was believed, why, by whom, under which authority, when, based on what evidence, what changed, and what was verified.

rows.anchor: Event ... State ... CurrentState = f(EventHistory).
rows.statement: Distinguishes Event ('deployment occurred') from State ('service is currently running version 5'), both needed; CurrentState = f(EventHistory); evidence is often event-derived (DeploymentEvent -> Observation -> Evidence), giving a temporal foundation for the feedback loop.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Semantic + Temporal + Epistemic + Governance.
rows.statement: States the information model must support three (later four) dimensions: Semantic (what does this mean?), Temporal (when was it true?), Epistemic (why should we believe it?), and Governance (who is authorized to make it authoritative?) — arriving at KnowledgeOS = Semantic+Temporal+Epistemic+Governance as 'the fundamental information architecture.'

rows.anchor: Identity, Type, Provenance, Producer, EpistemicStatus, Validity, Version, Authority
rows.statement: Proposes a common metadata envelope (Identity, Type, Provenance, Producer, EpistemicStatus, Validity, Version, Authority) shared across many objects, but warns against over-generalizing into one giant universal object/table since domain-specific semantics (Decision.Choice vs. Observation.ObservedState) must not be erased — the better approach is CommonIdentity/Provenance plus TypeSpecificSemantics, aligned with DDD.

rows.anchor: InformationModel ≠ DatabaseSchema. ... InformationModel ≠ APIContract.
rows.statement: Distinguishes the information model (what does the organization need to know?) from the database model (how will we persist it?) and from the API contract (the API may expose projections like KnowledgeView/GovernanceView/EvidenceView).

rows.anchor: Authority → Decision → Expected Knowledge → [compare] → Observation → Evidence → Finding → Recommendation → Authorization → Action → Verification → Knowledge Update
rows.statement: Consolidates the preliminary conceptual information-model diagram, noting the ordering of Recommendation/Authorization depends on the specific workflow but the semantic relationships are now visible; states the core invariant: every material engineering claim, decision, action, and verification must be semantically traceable.

rows.anchor: Current state / Historical state / Authority / Provenance / Evidence / Governance / Engineering / Runtime / AI / Audit
rows.statement: Step 126 verdict: lists ten question categories the information model should be able to answer (current state, historical state, why authoritative, provenance, evidence, who decided, implementation, runtime conformance, why the agent recommended this, what knowledge/authorization existed at action time) as fundamentally different from document search; boxes the first conceptual model (Knowledge+Claim+Evidence+Observation+Finding+Decision+Authority+Action+Verification) governed by Provenance+Authority+EpistemicStatus+TemporalValidity, and the key result: KnowledgeOS must model relationships, not merely store artifacts.

rows.statement: The book frames the archaeology method as prerequisite to the architecture's credibility: the architecture's credibility rests on the method's discipline, and the method is reusable where the architecture may not be.

rows.anchor: It read it *historically*: 688 documents sorted into three sequential eras (root -> kernel -> formal), five methodological regimes identified inside the formal era
rows.statement: The reconstruction sorted 688 documents into three sequential eras (root, kernel, formal) and five methodological regimes inside the formal era (measure-theory crisis, question series, Gita/Sarathi, computational closures, step series), measuring each regime's vocabulary, evidence standard and turnover before extracting any concept; the governing question was 'what happened in here?' not 'what is true in here?'.

rows.anchor: The corpus is the unit of completion... The filesystem artifact is the record... Coverage is stated, never implied
rows.statement: Three structural rules governed the archaeology: the corpus is the unit of completion (a discovery is recorded, not a reason to stop reading); the filesystem artifact is the record (chat is only an execution report); coverage is stated, never implied (e.g. the kernel era's roughly one-in-twenty full-read depth is disclosed on every dependent claim).

rows.anchor: a claim registry, a decision registry, a contradiction registry... an experiment registry, and a semantic lineage map that tracked contested terms
rows.statement: The archaeology pass built five instruments: a claim registry, decision registry, contradiction registry (tensions mapped before resolution), experiment registry, and a semantic lineage map tracking contested terms (Zero, Omega, Sarathi, etc.) across regime boundaries, because in this corpus the same word rarely keeps the same meaning.

rows.anchor: historical fact, hypothesis, experiment, decision, alternative, abandoned, superseded -- and, crucially, PROCESS/PROMPT artifact
rows.statement: The archaeology classified every touched document into: historical fact, hypothesis, experiment, decision, alternative, abandoned, superseded, or PROCESS/PROMPT artifact -- a saved prompt inside the historical tree is not historical evidence, and a copy is never corroboration.

rows.anchor: AF-009: the corpus contains not one externally ratified decision. Everything in it is author-level exploration.
rows.statement: The pre-governance finding AF-009 states the corpus contains not one externally ratified decision -- everything in it is author-level exploration; authority entered the programme only downstream through recorded rulings (book Part II.3), which is precisely why the method insists the corpus is evidence of discovery and can never be authority for architecture.

rows.anchor: SOURCE RECORD ... HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION ... LATER INTERPRETATION ... CURRENT RATIFIED UNDERSTANDING (never projected backward)
rows.statement: Declares a mandatory four-level separation for every historical claim in the book -- Source Record, Historical Reconstruction, Later Interpretation, Current Ratified Understanding -- with the rule that the present architecture may never rewrite its own history, framed as the chapter's central content/governing law.

rows.anchor: 'The corpus is the unit of completion.' ... 'The filesystem artifact is the record.' ... 'Coverage is stated, never implied.'
rows.statement: States three structural session-control rules, each adopted only after a recorded failure of its absence: completion means reading the whole corpus (not stopping at an interesting find); the filesystem artifact, not a chat claim, is the record; and coverage must be explicitly stated, never implied -- illustrated by a '160/160 processed' report later found to reflect only ~3-5% full reading, corrected in the coverage report's own section 0, with the caveat inherited by every kernel-era claim in the book.

rows.anchor: Ω predates the crisis it is remembered by. ... The famous Zero is the youngest Zero. ... The rich status vocabulary is older than the ladder.
rows.statement: Three worked cases where the dated record contradicted the expected 'smooth story': Omega actually enters the record a day before the measure-theory crisis it is remembered as belonging to (AF-003); the Zero meta-principle/absence-lens senses (2026-08-22) predate the computable-gap sense (08-27), reversing the expected order (AF-004); and the rich epistemic status vocabulary is an inheritance from an earlier constitutional tradition, older than the admission ladder it appears to enrich (AF-006) -- each demonstrating the record overriding the more natural narrative.

rows.anchor: Each case has the same shape: the smooth story was available, the dated record said otherwise, and the record won. That — not any claim of perfect neutrality — is what this book means when it says the history was reconstructed rather than written.
rows.statement: States the chapter's core epistemological stance: 'reconstructed rather than written' history means the dated record was allowed to override the more natural, expected story wherever they conflicted, not that the reconstruction achieved perfect neutrality.

rows.anchor: Source record: dated files carrying three distinct usages ... Historical reconstruction: three senses, two contemporaneous and one later ... Later interpretation ... Currently ratified: a terminology register
rows.statement: Worked four-level trace of the term 'Zero' through the method: source files show three distinct dated usages (absence-lens, ratified meta-principle, later formal nine-valued discrepancy structure); reconstruction identifies three senses (two contemporaneous, one later); interpretation frames their shared refusal ('not-knowing is neither nothing nor falsehood') as explaining the recurrence without asserting identity; the currently-ratified terminology register keeps all three senses distinct and separately flags that the ratified summary compresses the nine-valued source as an open, pending-disposition finding.

rows.anchor: a governance error in which a recommendation was executed as if it were a ruling — caught, corrected, and preserved with both layers intact; ... a chapter edited after its conformance check and caught only at the next gate — the failure that produced the post-edit re-verification rule now binding th

sources.note: Reframes 'Knowledge Zero' as the deliberate zeroing/neutralization of selected dimensions of a multidimensional knowledge state K=(d_1,...,d_n) to construct a Focus_S(K) (attention restricted to S) versus a Surface(K) (all dimensions jointly observed) observational frame, where d_i=0 denotes 'no operative influence attributed to dimension i under the current frame', explicitly not ontological absence, not an algebraic identity element, and not proof of future irrelevance. Documents cross-dimensional interaction (a dimension zero in isolation but non-zero jointly), the non-commutativity candidate R(P_S(K)) != P_S(R(K)) between focused reasoning and observational focus, and repeatedly strips premature scalar 'determination_score' fields from the proposed KR-STATE-01 Axis C data schema in favor of raw typed observation records.

rows.anchor: Focus_S(K)=Projection_S(K) ... Surface(K)=Obs_{\{1,\ldots,n\}}(K)
rows.statement: Defines Focus_S(K) as the projection retaining only dimensions in S (others zeroed/neutralized) and Surface(K) as the full joint observation across all dimensions, with 'surface does not mean shallow'.

rows.anchor: d_1=0 when observed alone, but (d_1,d_2)\neq(0,d_2) under a relational observation. Then d_1 has no standalone contribution but has a relational contribution.
rows.statement: Identifies cross-dimensional interaction: a dimension zero in isolation but non-zero jointly, explicitly linked to KR-ZERO's higher-order eliminability finding.

rows.anchor: P_S(K) = (d_i')_{i=1}^n where d_i'=d_i if i in S, 0_{D_i} if i not in S ... 0_{D_i} represents the identity/neutral element of dimension D_i
rows.statement: Formalizes the projection operator P_S with omitted dimensions set to 0_{D_i}; immediately corrected within the same file: this over-claims an algebraic identity, and P_S should instead be defined as restrict(K,S) with omitted dimensions 'not observed' rather than replaced by an algebraic zero, preserving 'Projection != Algebraic Zero' until proven otherwise.

rows.anchor: \Delta Det = Det(Q,P_{S\cup\{j\}}K) - [Det(Q,P_SK)+Det(Q,P_{\{j\}}K)]
rows.statement: Proposes then retracts an additive Determination Coupling Differential (independent/synergistic/masking regimes): the additive/numeric assumption about Determine is premature, so the first experiment should use a qualitative Compare(...) classification instead of Delta-Det in R.

rows.anchor: R(P_S(K))\neq P_S(R(K)) ... That non-commutativity could itself be a major Knowledge Algebra phenomenon.
rows.statement: Poses the live question of whether reasoning operates on the projected state (focused reasoning, R(P_S(K))) or on the full state with only the view projected (observational focus, P_S(R(K))), proposing R.P_S =?= P_S.R as a foundational experiment.

rows.anchor: Determine(Q,Focus_S(K)) > Determine(Q,Surface(K)) ... More information \not\Rightarrow better epistemic determination.
rows.statement: Hypothesizes that a focused projection can sometimes yield better determination than the full surface view (deliberate neutralization reducing interference), connecting Zero, Focus and purification into one candidate pattern still requiring experimental confirmation.

rows.anchor: This field: "determination_score": {"type": "number", "minimum": 0.0, "maximum": 1.0} is premature.
rows.statement: Removes a scalar bounded 'determination_score' field from the proposed KR-STATE-01 Axis C schema, replacing it with a raw typed status enum (DETERMINED/UNDERDETERMINED/CONTRADICTED/UNKNOWN) to avoid assuming Determine is measurable, scalar and bounded.

rows.anchor: Zero and Focus are currently conflated ... Zero concerns influence: Influence_i(K|Q,C)=0. Focus concerns what we choose to make operative/observable: Focus_S(K).
rows.statement: Separates Zero (a claim about influence) from Focus/projection (a choice about what to observe), stating 'Projection may instantiate a Zero assumption' but Projection != Zero, and warning that a projected P_{1}(K)=(d_1,0,0) view must not be read as proving d_2=d_3=0 in the underlying state.

rows.anchor: d_i=0 \Longleftrightarrow the influence of dimension i is treated as neutralized under the current model. This is different from saying d_i=\varnothing or d_i does not exist.
rows.statement: Defines 0_i as 'no operative influence attributed to dimension i under the specified frame' rather than absence of the dimension, applied to a worked example K^{(1,3)}=(d_1,0,d_3,0).

rows.anchor: We must never silently convert assumed zero influence into proven zero influence. There should be a distinction: Zero^{assumed}_i versus Zero^{observed}_i versus potentially Zero^{validated}_i.
rows.statement: Distinguishes assumed/observed/validated Zero: a projection P_S(K) creates only an assumed/constructed zero, and only agreement of Determine(Q,P_S(K)) with the full state gives evidence the zeroing was adequate.

rows.anchor: 0^t \rightarrow 0^{t+1} \rightarrow +^{t+2} because its influence becomes operative after the knowledge substrate changes.
rows.statement: Connects dimensional-Zero-as-modeling-assumption to the temporal re-basing thread: a dimension's influence status can transition 0->0->non-zero across states, giving the conceptual chain 'dimension exists -> influence neutralized -> focus created -> reasoning occurs -> knowledge rebases -> previously neutralized dimension may become operative'.

rows.statement: Corrects the claim that 0_{D_i} is an identity/neutral element: proposes P_S(K)=restrict(K,S) with omitted dimensions 'not observed' rather than replaced by an algebraic zero, preserving 'Projection != Algebraic Zero' pending a later derived structure.

rows.anchor: Does reasoning operate on the projected state, or does projection merely determine what is observed while reasoning still has access to the full state? ... R(P_S(K))\neq P_S(R(K))
rows.statement: Poses focused-reasoning versus observational-focus as a fundamental architectural question, proposing R.P_S =?= P_S.R as a candidate major Knowledge Algebra experiment.

rows.statement: Restates 'Knowledge Zero' as a vector of per-dimension neutral states rather than a scalar zero, cautioning against fixing 1/0 polarity before the experiment specifies it.

rows.statement: Distinguishes the knowledge state from an observation view of it, so a change in focused view across time (S_t != S_{t+1}) need not signal contradiction in the underlying knowledge.

rows.statement: Proposes a KR-STATE-01 Axis C protocol: construct controlled projections P_S(K) over dimension subsets S, measuring preserved/lost/newly-visible determination and cross-dimensional interaction.

sources.note: A large alternative Step-289 research mandate (self-marked 'superseded by 2303 tightening' in its own filename) proposing an operations-focused programme -- investigating what a KnowledgeOS operation is, operation identity independent of state identity, five candidate operation-carrier formalizations, operation composition properties (associativity/identity/closure/commutativity, none assumed), a minimum transition contract for delta, and a controlled Gita Karma/Phala corroboration hypothesis -- with sixteen planned executable tests (T289-01..T289-16) and thirteen planned deliverable files. Not the mandate actually executed in this batch (S2147's dependency-graph/bootstrap-boundary mandate was instead), but its core structural-transfer-forbidden principle (no operation algebra from Sigma-order or Policy-lattice) generalizes the programme's recurring discipline to a third domain.

rows.anchor: Step 289 should not attempt to "solve the kernel." Its purpose should be to investigate and formally constrain the **operation space** over the ratified $K_t$ ... **Step 289 must derive the candidate operation model; it must not assume an operation algebra merely because policy composition or the $\Sigma$-model has an algebraic structure.**
rows.statement: Proposes an alternative Step 289 scope focused on constraining the operation space O over the ratified K_t (rather than a dependency-graph/bootstrap analysis), with the central correction that Step 289 must derive a candidate operation model rather than assuming an operation algebra merely because policy composition or the Sigma model happens to have an algebraic structure -- explicitly listing non-goals: do not ratify the operation registry, select the kernel, define equality, decide Pi-in-equiv, select the observational axis subset X, define provenance relevance, define Sigma's component orders, invent primitives, or promote Gita concepts into architecture.

rows.anchor: ### First distinction: operation ≠ transition ... $$o : I \rightarrow O$$ ... without yet establishing that it is a state transition: $$\delta : K \times \mathcal O \rightarrow K.$$ ... Only the last property makes it directly a state-transforming operation.
rows.statement: Poses operation-vs-transition as a first category distinction to be tested, not assumed: an operation o:I->O (accepting input, producing a result, possibly inspecting state, producing evidence, requesting authority) is not automatically the same as a state-transforming operation delta:K x O -> K; only operations with the state-transforming property are directly state transitions. Proposes (as an untested research hypothesis, not a canonical claim) partitioning O into O_read, O_derive, O_transform, and O_govern.
missing: corpus evidence for or against the read/derive/transform/govern partition

rows.anchor: ### A. Operation as command ... ### B. Operation as typed command ... ### C. Operation as transition witness ... ### D. Operation as partial transformation ... ### E. Operation as governed transition ... These are **candidate models only**.
rows.statement: Proposes five candidate formal carriers for an 'operation', explicitly as untested candidates rather than a chosen model: (A) operation as command o:K->K'; (B) operation as typed command o:(I,K)->Result; (C) operation as transition witness o:(K,I)->(K',E) recording transition evidence E; (D) operation as partial transformation o:K x I -\-> K, undefined for invalid inputs; (E) operation as governed transition o:(K,I,P,A) -\-> (K',E) with policy P and authority A participating explicitly. States the research task is to determine which structure, if any, the corpus actually supports.
missing: which of the five candidate carrier models the corpus supports

rows.anchor: State identity cannot be reused as operation identity without proof. ... Candidate fields to audit include: operation type, operation name, operation version, ... The central question: $o_1 = o_2$ means what? This must remain distinct from: $\delta(K,o_1)=\delta(K,o_2).$
rows.statement: Mandates that operation identity be researched as its own object, not reused from state identity, since Step 288 already showed state identity (id=H(P,e,c,t,Pi)) does not automatically provide operation identity. Requires a twelve-field candidate audit (operation type, name, version, instance, actor, authority act, input, target state, policy, timestamp, causal predecessor, provenance, result) each classified by possible identity role, and insists 'o1=o2' must remain a distinct question from 'delta(K,o1)=delta(K,o2)' -- the earlier policy-level equality-vs-equal-output distinction is evidence only at the policy level and must not be automatically generalized to K_t.
missing: a corpus-grounded definition of operation identity
invariants: state identity cannot be reused as operation identity without independent proof

rows.anchor: A particularly important possibility is: $o_1 \neq o_2 \quad\land\quad \delta(K,o_1)=\delta(K,o_2).$ If this exists, then state effect does not establish operation identity. Conversely: $o_1 \neq o_2 \quad\land\quad Obs(\delta(K,o_1)) = Obs(\delta(K,o_2))$ would establish that observational equality is even coarser.
rows.statement: Poses four operation-level relations (structural equality o1=o2, semantic equivalence o1≡_O o2, behavioural equivalence o1≈_O o2, and provenance-sensitive equivalence o1≅_{λ,O} o2 -- names explicitly flagged as not to be promoted) as candidates to test for whether the corpus already distinguishes them, and highlights two specific hypothesis-shaped possibilities requiring testing rather than assertion: distinct operations producing the same state effect (would show state effect does not establish operation identity) and distinct operations producing the same observable effect (would show observational equality is coarser still than state-effect equality).

rows.anchor: ### 23. Operation algebra must not be borrowed from Σ ... $(\Sigma,\preceq) \Rightarrow (\mathcal O,\circ).$ There is no such implication. Likewise: $(\mathcal P,\land) \Rightarrow (\mathcal O,\land).$ There is no such implication. ... $$\boxed{\Sigma\text{-structure} \qquad Policy\text{-structure} \qquad Operation\text{-structure}}$$
rows.statement: Generalizes the programme's recurring illegitimate-structural-transfer discipline to a third domain: explicitly forbids inferring an operation-composition algebra (O, compose) from either the Sigma product-order (Sigma, <=) or the Policy meet-semilattice (Policy, and) -- three algebraic domains (Sigma-structure, Policy-structure, Operation-structure) must remain separate until a formal homomorphism or other relationship is independently demonstrated. Also explicitly forbids inferring operation composition semantics (o2 composed with o1 as sequential execution) unless the relevant transition semantics formally establish that delta(delta(K,o1),o2) equals delta(K, o2-composed-with-o1).
invariants: no algebraic structure transfers between Sigma, Policy, and Operation domains without independent proof

rows.anchor: ### 26. Minimum transition contract ... $$\boxed{(K,o,Pre,Policy,Authority,Identity,Equality,Result,Failure)}$$ but this is a **candidate dependency set**, not a canonical contract.
rows.statement: Proposes identifying the minimum information contract required before delta:K_t x O -\-> K_t could be derived, offering a candidate (not canonical) nine-field dependency set -- (K, o, Precondition, Policy, Authority, Identity, Equality, Result, Failure) -- each to be individually classified ESTABLISHED/DERIVABLE/NORMATIVE/TECHNICALLY OPEN/BLOCKED/DEFERRED, with the eventual dependency graph (K_t branching into ontology, identity, equality, policy, authority, observation, and operation, the latter further branching into preconditions/postconditions/composition/failure/replay/determinism feeding into delta) to be checked for cycles using the same derivation-vs-governance discipline as the (superseding) dependency-graph mandate.
missing: a ratified minimum transition contract

rows.anchor: ### 28. Gītā track — controlled philosophical lens ... Does the Gītā's distinction between action and its result provide a useful philosophical corroboration of the already independently derived distinction between an operation and its resulting state? ... $$\boxed{\text{Gītā correspondence} \not\Rightarrow \text{KnowledgeOS operation semantics}}$$
rows.statement: Proposes the Bhagavad Gita's Karma/Phala (action/result) distinction as a controlled, corroboration-only hypothesis lens for the already-independently-derived Command != Transformation distinction, explicitly prohibiting the identities Karma=Operation or Phala=State, and prohibiting use of the Gita to derive operation primitives, operation identity, transition semantics, authority model, policy model, or kernel structure -- the strongest acceptable result is stated to be corroboration, never derivation, restating the Step-286 discipline that 'philosophy may illuminate a distinction; engineering must establish it.'
invariants: philosophy may illuminate a distinction; engineering must establish it

rows.anchor: It must not conclude: "Operations form a monoid." ... "Operations form a semigroup." ... "Every operation is a state transition." ... "Successful operation means knowledge growth." ... "Operation equality follows from equal state output." ... "Gītā's Karma defines the KnowledgeOS operation." This is explicitly forbidden.
rows.statement: Enumerates six explicit forbidden conclusions for the (superseded) operations research: operations form a monoid (unless closure/associativity/identity independently demonstrated); operations form a semigroup (unless closure/associativity demonstrated); every operation is a state transition (unless corpus-established); successful operation means knowledge growth (unless a formal K-Sigma relation is established); operation equality follows from equal state output (unless equality and injectivity conditions are established); and Gita's Karma defines the KnowledgeOS operation (explicitly and unconditionally forbidden).

rows.anchor: I would make **one important strategic change** compared with the way Steps 285–288 evolved. Do **not** make Step 289 another attempt to solve everything around operations. The dependency should be: Step 285 -> Step 287/288 -> **Step 289: operation boundary** -> Step 290: rejection/authority -> Step 291: δ
rows.statement: Proposes an alternative programme sequencing (Step 285 -> Steps 287/288 -> Step 289 operation boundary -> Step 290 rejection/authority -> Step 291 delta) with equality kept as an explicit ongoing dependency, framing Step 289 as reconnaissance/formalization for O rather than a final operation-contract step. This sequencing is superseded: the batch's actually-executed Step 289 (S2147-S2162) instead pursued dependency-graph/bootstrap-boundary analysis, and this file's own name records it as superseded by a 23:03 tightening.

lineage_claims.target: this file itself, per its own filename 'superseded-by-2303-tightening'
lineage_claims.quote: superseded-by-2303-tightening

rows.anchor: **Step 288 has deliberately *not* closed equality, and therefore Step 289 must not silently assume a final equality relation in order to define operations.** ... The right task is therefore to define the **operation universe and typed operation semantics independently of choosing final equality**, and to mark exactly where each operation is blocked by unresolved equality/identity.
rows.statement: Restates the central design constraint for this tightened mandate: since Step 288 deliberately left equality open, Step 289's operation research must not silently assume a final equality relation; instead it should define the operation universe and typed operation semantics independently of choosing equality, explicitly marking wherever a given operation is blocked by unresolved equality/identity questions, per a four-stage flow (operation semantics -> operation/equality dependency analysis -> identify equality-dependent portions -> do not choose equality).
invariants: operation semantics research must not silently assume a chosen equality relation

lineage_claims.quote: Step 289 should be tightened before execution.

rows.anchor: ### 1. Do not make `𝒪_core` the starting assumption ... ### 2. Separate four different things: operation name ≠ operation type ≠ operation semantics ≠ membership in O_core ... ### 4. Separate `𝒪`, `𝒪_core`, and `𝒯` ... $$𝒪_{all}, 𝒪_{sem}, 𝒪_{impl}, 𝒪_{norm}, 𝒪_{core}, 𝒯$$
rows.statement: Specifies four of six named improvements over the prior operations mandate: (1) the question must be 'what operation universe is actually evidenced, and which subset if any is O_core' rather than assuming O_core as a starting point; (2) every operation must be classified across four independent axes -- name, type, semantics, and O_core-membership -- since e.g. Reject could be a decision, state transition, governance action, or event-producing command depending on actual corpus semantics, never decided from its name alone; (4) six candidate operation-related sets must be defined and empirically tested for their actual relationships rather than assumed: O_all (every operation-like construct found), O_sem (operations with semantic effect), O_impl (implemented operations), O_norm (normatively required operations), O_core (the indispensable subset), and T (the transformation family, if mathematically justified).

rows.anchor: ### 5. Add a genuine operation-minimality test ... `O_core' = O_core \ {o}` and test whether a mandatory capability becomes unrepresentable. But also test **replacement**: Can `o` be replaced by a composition of other operations? Otherwise two aliases could falsely appear to be two independent primitives.
rows.statement: Adds a two-part operation-minimality test as the fifth named improvement: a deletion test (remove candidate operation o from O_core and check whether a mandatory capability becomes unrepresentable) combined with a replacement test (check whether o can instead be expressed as a composition of other already-required operations) -- the replacement test is required specifically because a deletion test alone could not distinguish a genuine independent primitive from an alias of another operation composed differently.

rows.anchor: ### 6. Add a strong anti-prematurity gate ... choosing final `K`; choosing final equality; declaring `𝒯` complete merely because all known operations were found; declaring `𝒪_core` minimal without deletion/replacement tests; treating implementation operations as domain operations; treating events as transformations merely because they occur after transformations; importing philosophical concepts as operations; deriving mathematical structure from the Bhagavad Gītā.
rows.statement: Specifies the sixth named improvement, an eight-item anti-prematurity gate explicitly prohibiting: choosing a final K; choosing a final equality relation; declaring T complete merely because every currently-known operation was catalogued; declaring O_core minimal without both deletion and replacement tests; treating implementation-level operations as domain operations; treating events as transformations merely because they temporally follow transformations; importing philosophical concepts directly as operations; and deriving mathematical structure from the Bhagavad Gita -- the philosophy lane remains corroborative only, per the Step-286 discipline.

rows.anchor: ### A. State transformation $T : K \times I \rightharpoonup K$ ### B. History transformation ... ### C. Assessment ... ### D. Query ... ### E. Event construction ... ### F. History reconstruction ... ### G. Projection ... ### H. Governance predicate ... ### I. Decision ... ### J. Policy composition ... ### K. Equality/equivalence test ... Do not assume these categories are exhaustive.
rows.statement: Specifies an eleven-category typed operation taxonomy (explicitly non-exhaustive, extensible only when corpus evidence requires it) to classify every candidate operation: state transformation T:KxI-\->K; history transformation T_H:HxI-\->H; assessment A:KxX->Assessment; query Q:KxI->Result; event construction E:OperationResult->Event; history reconstruction R:H->K; projection P:K->Y; governance predicate G:KxContextxAuthorityxPolicy->{Allow,Reject}; decision D:AssessmentxPolicyxAuthority->Decision; policy composition C:PolicyxPolicy->Policy; and equality/equivalence test Eq:XxX->{True,False,Unknown} -- requiring every candidate to be checked against all eleven rather than forced into the single state-transition form T:K->K.

rows.anchor: operation dependence does not imply state membership. ... For example: `Replay` may reconstruct state without itself being a state mutation.
rows.statement: States a specific corpus-derived principle: operation dependence on state does not imply state membership -- an operation that reads or depends on K is not thereby itself a member of the state or a state mutation. Illustrated with Replay, which may reconstruct state without itself being a state mutation, and generalized into a required checklist for every operation (whether it changes K, changes H, creates an Event/Assessment/Decision, changes governance state, reads K, reads H, or projects K), with an operation permitted to belong to several categories simultaneously.
invariants: operation dependence on state does not imply state membership

rows.anchor: # 15. DISTINGUISH DOMAIN OPERATIONS FROM IMPLEMENTATION OPERATIONS ... Would this operation still exist if the implementation technology changed? ... Do not promote infrastructure mechanisms into the KnowledgeOS ontology merely because the implementation uses them.
rows.statement: Mandates a domain-vs-implementation classification test for every candidate operation via the DDD-discipline question 'would this operation still exist if the implementation technology changed?' -- explicitly warning this is evidence, not proof -- and requires infrastructure-level mechanisms (repository operations, serialization, hashing, database transactions, locking, caching, indexing, message publishing, event persistence, API calls) to never be promoted into the KnowledgeOS domain ontology merely because a given implementation happens to use them.

rows.anchor: # 26. DEPENDENCY GRAPH ... Classify every edge as: definition / dependency / constraint / derivation / implementation dependency / governance dependency. Do not render a definition as a two-way dependency. A prerequisite is not necessarily a member of the dependent structure.
rows.statement: Requires a dependency graph over fourteen named concepts (Equality, Identity, Operation, Transformation, History, Policy, Authority, Governance, Observation, K, H, delta, O, T) with edges classified into six types (definition, dependency, constraint, derivation, implementation dependency, governance dependency), explicitly incorporating the lesson from the meanwhile-executed dependency-graph work: a definition must never be rendered as a two-way dependency edge, and a prerequisite is not necessarily a member of the dependent structure it constrains.
invariants: a definitional equation must not be rendered as a two-way dependency edge
a prerequisite is not necessarily a member of the structure it constrains

sources.note: S0893's Step 25C.1: a twelve-scenario test suite evaluates five candidate frameworks (Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, Qualitative/set-based, Weighted scoring, Fuzzy logic) against ten requirements; concludes the qualitative algebra is the PRIMARY KERNEL CANDIDATE while Bayesian/D-S become pluggable specialized contexts and weighted-scoring/fuzzy are REJECTED/not-the-kernel; delivers the final architectural decision (framework-independent kernel + pluggable inference engines) and the 'AI may propose; Kernel must determine' principle; hands off to Step 25C.2 (Independent Evidence Combination).

rows.anchor: We now do the comparison rather than choosing a framework by preference. What mathematical machinery should KnowledgeOS use to aggregate evidence? My recommendation is to evaluate candidates against the actual requirements we have derived, not against abstract elegance.
rows.statement: States the method for Step 25C.1: evaluate candidate evidence-aggregation frameworks against derived requirements, not abstract elegance or preference.

rows.statement: Defines a common twelve-scenario test suite (one hypothesis H, twelve evidence conditions) for evaluating candidate aggregation frameworks, noting failing a requirement doesn't make a framework useless, only disqualifies it as the universal kernel.

rows.statement: Proposes a five-layer mathematical stack diagram (Knowledge Kernel → Evidence Graph → Epistemic Assessment → Inference Engines → Decision Math), more powerful than choosing one epistemic mathematics for everything.

rows.anchor: What should be deterministic? ... EvidenceIdentity, ProvenanceResolution, TemporalValidity, ConflictDetection, DependencyTraversal, KnowledgeRevision, EpistemicContractEvaluation. rows.anchor: But we still have one critical mathematical hole ... If two independent pieces of evidence support the same proposition, how much stronger does the proposition become? sources.note: S0855's Step 1: operationalizes independence as a three-valued, policy-relative, six-dimension-vector function over evidence metadata and provenance graphs; explicitly distinguishes operational from statistical independence; sets up Step 2 (evidence identity/equivalence calculus).

rows.anchor: Can KnowledgeOS determine whether two evidence items are independent using computable information? ... True Independence ... Operationally Established Independence ... KnowledgeOS cannot generally prove metaphysical independence. It can determine independence relative to an explicit evidence model.
rows.statement: Distinguishes True (metaphysical) Independence, which KnowledgeOS cannot generally prove, from Operationally Established Independence, which it can determine relative to an explicit evidence model; defines Ind_ρ(e_i,e_j,G,C)→{Independent,Dependent,Unknown} over evidence pair, provenance graph G, context C, and independence policy ρ.

type_signature.domain: Evidence x Evidence x Graph x Context

rows.anchor: What information can KnowledgeOS actually inspect? ... M(e)=(Source,AcquisitionEvent,Timestamp,Actor,Method,ParentEvidence,Transformation,Location,Content,Context)
rows.statement: Defines the inspectable evidence-metadata tuple M(e)=(Source, AcquisitionEvent, Timestamp, Actor, Method, ParentEvidence, Transformation, Location, Content, Context), illustrated by contrasting a direct Nexus-API observation with an LLM summarization whose Parent is that observation.

rows.anchor: The first deterministic rule ... If e_i\leadsto e_j in the provenance graph, then Ind(e_i,e_j)=Dependent. This is deterministic. No LLM is required.
rows.statement: States a deterministic rule requiring no LLM: if e_i leads to e_j in the provenance graph (e.g. Database → LLM extraction), then Ind(e_i,e_j)=Dependent.

rows.anchor: Common ancestry ... CommonAncestor(A,B)=D ... we cannot safely say A\perp B ... CommonAncestor(e_i,e_j) \Rightarrow Independent(e_i,e_j)\neq Confirmed ... The result should normally be Unknown unless the policy provides a justified way to establish conditional independence.
rows.statement: For two evidence items with no direct edge but a common ancestor (e.g. two LLMs, A and B, both reading Document D), states CommonAncestor(e_i,e_j) ⇒ Independent(e_i,e_j)≠Confirmed, with the default result Unknown unless the policy justifies conditional independence.

rows.anchor: Different sources do not automatically mean independent ... Reuters → Document A, Reuters → Document B ... Source(A)\neq Source(B) does not prove A\perp B ... DifferentSource\not\Rightarrow Independent
rows.statement: Warns that different apparent sources (e.g. two documents both ultimately from Reuters) do not prove independence, since both may originate from the same underlying report: DifferentSource ⇏ Independent.

rows.anchor: Different acquisition events are stronger ... Sensor A → 20°C at 10:00, Sensor B → 20°C at 10:00 ... independent sensors; independent acquisition mechanisms; independent provenance; no shared upstream observation. Then we can establish OperationallyIndependent(e_1,e_2) under the declared policy. Not
rows.statement: Shows that independent acquisition mechanisms/provenance (e.g. two separate sensors reporting the same 20°C reading with no shared upstream observation) can establish OperationallyIndependent(e1,e2) under a declared policy, stressing the qualifier 'operationally'.

rows.anchor: We therefore need an independence evidence vector ... I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) ... Source independence ... Acquisition independence ... Provenance independence ... Method independence ... Temporal independence ... Common-ancestor status ... Each can be {Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown}. This
rows.statement: Proposes representing independence not as a single boolean but as a six-dimension vector I(e_i,e_j)=(i_S,i_A,i_P,i_M,i_T,i_C) — Source, Acquisition, Provenance, Method, Temporal independence and Common-ancestor status — each valued {Confirmed,Rejected,Unknown}, to preserve uncertainty.

rows.anchor: Why not simply calculate an independence score? We should resist IndependenceScore=0.87 because that number would obscure why the evidence is considered independent. ... This is much more auditable.
rows.statement: Argues against collapsing independence into a single score like IndependenceScore=0.87, since a scalar obscures why evidence is considered independent, in favor of an itemized per-dimension Confirmed/Rejected breakdown that is auditable.

rows.anchor: Formal decision rule ... Ind_\rho(e_i,e_j,G,C) = Dependent if dependency is established; Independent if all required independence conditions hold; Unknown otherwise. The important word is required ... because the conditions depend on policy. For a high-risk security decision, we may require very str
rows.statement: Gives the formal decision rule for Ind_ρ as a three-way case split (Dependent/Independent/Unknown) keyed on policy-defined 'required' conditions, noting the required strength of independence is itself policy-dependent (e.g. stronger for high-risk security decisions than exploratory research).

rows.anchor: The three-valued result is important ... I=\{I,D,U\} ... better than {True,False} because Unknown\neq False and Unknown\neq True. ... Absence of evidence for independence is not evidence of dependence, but neither is it evidence of independence.
rows.statement: Argues the three-valued result set {Independent, Dependent, Unknown} is necessary rather than a boolean, since Unknown≠False and Unknown≠True, stating the central KnowledgeOS principle: 'Absence of evidence for independence is not evidence of dependence, but neither is it evidence of independence.'

rows.anchor: DDD representation ... IndependenceAssessment ... EvidenceA, EvidenceB, SourceRelation, AcquisitionRelation, ProvenanceRelation, MethodRelation, CommonAncestor, Result, Policy, Basis, Timestamp ... The result is a domain object, not merely a database flag.
rows.statement: Models the independence determination as an IndependenceAssessment domain object (EvidenceA/B, per-dimension relation fields, CommonAncestor, Result, Policy, Basis, Timestamp) rather than a bare database flag.

rows.anchor: Domain invariant ... Dependent(e_i,e_j) \Rightarrow \neg Independent(e_i,e_j) ... Unknown(e_i,e_j) \Rightarrow \neg ConfirmedIndependent(e_i,e_j). The second is particularly important.
rows.statement: States two formal invariants: Dependent(e_i,e_j) ⇒ ¬Independent(e_i,e_j), and Unknown(e_i,e_j) ⇒ ¬ConfirmedIndependent(e_i,e_j), flagging the second as particularly important.

rows.anchor: Test cases ... Case A — Exact duplicate ... Dependent/SameContribution ... Case B — LLM transformation ... Dependent ... Case C — Two LLMs reading the same document ... Unknown ... Case D — Two independent sensors ... Independent ... Case E — Two websites copying the same source ... Dependent/Correl
rows.statement: Works six test cases through Ind_ρ: (A) exact duplicate → Dependent/SameContribution; (B) e2=LLM(e1) → Dependent; (C) two LLMs reading the same document D → Unknown (absent a conditional-independence policy); (D) two independent sensors → Independent under policy; (E) two websites copying one source → Dependent/Correlated; (F) missing provenance → Unknown.

rows.anchor: This gives us an important KnowledgeOS law ... Independence must be established, not assumed. ... Independence(e_i,e_j)=Confirmed only when the declared policy's conditions are satisfied. Otherwise Unknown.
rows.statement: Provisionally adopts the KnowledgeOS law 'Independence must be established, not assumed', formalized as Independence(e_i,e_j)=Confirmed only when the declared policy's conditions are satisfied, else Unknown.

rows.anchor: One subtle statistical correction ... Operational independence is not necessarily statistical independence. ... both may be affected by the same environmental bias. OperationallyIndependent \not\Rightarrow StatisticallyIndependent ... OperationalIndependence \rightarrow Evidence about possible stati
rows.statement: Introduces a key caveat: OperationallyIndependent does not imply StatisticallyIndependent (e.g. two sensors with separate acquisition/hardware may still share an environmental bias); operational independence only provides evidence about possible statistical independence, and a Bayesian factorization P(E1,E2|H)=P(E1|H)P(E2|H) needs its own justified assumptions — hence Evidence Architecture and Statistical Inference Policy must be kept separate.

rows.anchor: Step 1 conclusion ... operational independence is computable in a qualified sense. ... it must not claim universal statistical independence merely from metadata.
rows.statement: Concludes Step 1: KnowledgeOS can deterministically inspect provenance, dependency, common ancestry, acquisition events, sources, methods, and context to produce Independent/Dependent/Unknown under a declared policy, but must never claim universal statistical independence from metadata alone.

rows.anchor: Step 2 ... How does KnowledgeOS determine whether two evidence items are the same underlying evidential contribution, merely semantically equivalent, or genuinely distinct observations? That takes us into the Evidence Identity / Equivalence Calculus ... I suggest we tackle that next—and test it with
rows.statement: Closes by posing Step 2's question — same underlying evidential contribution vs semantic equivalence vs genuinely distinct observation — as the Evidence Identity/Equivalence Calculus, to be tackled next via concrete examples rather than abstract definition; taken up by the immediately following file.
